not loaded: the bitmap at $4000 past the start-up, where the 3D view and the menus are drawn; the checksum leaves it out, and at the hand-over it holds zeros and, from $4307, bytes the loader left
not loaded: rows of the bitmap at $4000 between the tables at $4F00 and $5780; the checksum leaves them out, and at the hand-over they hold the RAM's power-on pattern
not loaded: the league's 192 bytes, made by NEW_LEAGUE and saved and loaded with a game; the checksum leaves them out, and at the hand-over they hold the RAM's power-on pattern
not loaded: work tables the game fills while it runs; the checksum leaves them out, and at the hand-over they hold the RAM's power-on pattern

not loaded: the tables the start-up copies here from the bitmaps' area (described where they are loaded, at $5780 and $63E0-$7648) and the game's variables from $C300; the checksum leaves them out, and at the hand-over they are zeros

comments.text: The processor port's direction register, $2F from the reset on: the game never writes it.
Tape (0) or disc (1), as the menu leaves it (MENU_LOAD_SAVE). SAVE_OR_LOAD takes the device number for SETLFS from $2C21 plus this, 1 or 8, and DISK_COMMAND does nothing while it is 0.

One step of the world, called once a pass in the race (and twice while the car is lowered at the start): the car's physics, the opponent, the wheels against the road, the forces and the moves. The step takes longer than a frame, so between its parts it calls FLIP_IF_READY, which finishes the switch to the newly drawn bitmap as soon as the interrupt has made it. The second half (springs, drag, torques) runs only once $C307 is set, when the car is on its wheels.

Where the car's three points of contact (the two front wheels and the back) sit from its middle, from the rotation matrix: the first two are row $22 (and row $23 for the other axis) less and plus half the sum of rows $1F and $1A (half the difference of rows $1C and $21), the third is row $22 (row $23) negated. Low bytes at $0130-$0132 and $0136-$0138, high bytes three on.

Moves the car by its velocity: each axis of the position ($0100-$0108, three bytes an axis) by a quarter of its velocity ($0109/$010F), upwards by a half; the height is kept below $03E8. Turns the three angles ($0121/$0124) by their speeds ($016A/$016D), keeping the pitch and the roll within the limits at $0A55 and $0A57 (the second pair, wider, while $C373 and $C359 say the car is coming down from a jump): one that hits its limit stops turning that way. Sets $C3DC bit 7 when the roll is past 15, and $33/$69 to $3C less the pitch over 32.
The highest pitch and roll MOVE_CAR allows ($2C), and the higher one while landing ($0A).
The lowest pitch and roll ($D3), and while landing ($F5).
Adds each of the three forces ($0115/$011B) to its axis of the velocity ($0109/$010F).
Adds each of the three torques ($0118/$011E) to its axis of the spin ($010C/$0112).

For each point of contact, X from 2 to 0: how far it is down into the road, the road's height at $C340/$C343/$C3CE less the point's at $C346/$C349/$C3D1, less $0E (0, and 2 once the car is wrecked, so that it sinks), kept at $0179/$017C/$C3D4. A point more than $300 above the road (its top two bytes below $FFFD) is off it and its spring's press is 0; otherwise the depth, its middle byte held at $14 at most, gives the press ($0148/$014B): the depth plus its change since the last step (ADD16_18, the last kept at $0142/$0145), never below 0 and held at $11FF. A press reaching 4 in its high byte when it was below 2 counts a landing at $C3BC. A press reaching $C38B plus 7 damages the car while $E1, which counts such presses in a row across the three points and from step to step and is cleared by any press under the line, is still below $209B: its excess over $C38B plus 6, at most $7F, and half again is added to the point's damage at $C3C3 (held at $FF), and $C352 is set; the largest over $C38B is kept at $C35C. Then the springs' mean $0160/$0161 (points 0 and 1 a quarter each, point 2 a half), WHEEL_LEVERS, three times the difference of points 0 and 1 held to 16 either way ($0166/$0167, the roll's force), and the mean of points 0 and 1 less point 2's ($014E/$014F, the pitch's); $6A is non-zero while that mean is ($0160 OR $0161). With it 0 and the car not hanging from the crane ($2F), the pitch's force is held at a limit set by the pitch and the track. Then the crane (CRANE), the bump's pushes taken in (OPP_PUSH) and, on a landing, sound effect 3.

The forces the road puts on the car through the springs: $015B (upwards, from $013D and $0171), $015C (sideways: the sideways speed $0150, worn down by $0159 while both are positive and held to what the road can take, plus $0172 and $013E), and the pull along the road (SIDE_GRIP).

The torques: about the first axis ($0118/$011E), the pitch's force ($014E) less a sixteenth of the spin, plus a quarter of the sideways force ($015C) while on the road; about the third ($011A/$0120), the roll's force ($0166) less a sixteenth of the spin.

The force along the road ($015A/$015D): the spring's ($013C plus $0170) less the speed along it ($0154/$0157), held to what the road can take (ROAD_HOLD); $C3C6 is set to $80 when it was held, as the wheels slide.
How hard the road can push, in $14/$15: twice the spring's force $0171/$0174 while any spring is pressed and that force is positive, else 0.

Takes a share of the velocity from the forces, $C350 parts in 256 shifted right by 2, 4 or 6 places. On the road the share is the largest of the three speeds along the road ($0154-$0159), less 20 while the boost ($C308) is on with the engine running ($C36A); otherwise $C0: a fixed share shifted 2 places when the car is skidding sideways ($E4 past 2) or wrecked ($6B), 4 places when it hangs from the crane or $0E is set.

Divides the three points' heights by 8; from their differences, the sines of the car's pitch ($0178, with bit 7 flipped) and roll ($0176), and their cosines through COSINE_OF; then the springs' mean force along each axis of the car ($0170-$0175), by those sines and cosines.
The size of the signed sixteen bits in A and $14, as a byte ($FF from 256 up), in $56, and from the table at $B080 the cosine of an angle with that sine, in $57.

Once a pass of the race: runs down $82, the passes left of showing the last lap's time, and puts the best lap back when it ends; moves both cars' lap clocks on by a pass and checks each for a lap (LAP_CHECK); checks for the race's end (LAPS_DONE); and runs the countdown at $6C (twice a pass while $C373 bit 7 is set).

Runs the countdown at $6C, while it is from 1 to $7F: down by one each pass the car is off the road or hanging from the crane, or while it is 6 or more. Bit 2 of it goes to $C399, for a flashing lamp. When it reaches 0 it becomes $80 and $C351 is set.
Compares lap clock X with clock Y, minutes ($8398), seconds ($82B0) and hundredths ($8298), all in decimal: when X's time is the shorter it is copied over Y's, and the carry comes back clear.
Sets the lamp for the best lap and draws the best lap's time (clock 2) in the dashboard's fourth place, with its hundredths. X is kept.

Counts a lap for car X (0 the player, 1 the opponent): when its piece ($C374) is the one the start line is on ($C77C), and $C376 bit 7 is clear (cleared once the car has passed piece $C767, half way round), $C378 goes up by one and $C376 bit 7 is set. For the player the lap number is drawn, and from the second lap on the lap's time shows for 25 passes. A lap faster than the best becomes the best (FASTER), and when it was the opponent's it shows with its lamp. Then the car's lap clock starts again from 0.

Ends the race when either car has run its laps ($C378 equal to $C354) and it has not ended ($C364): the countdown starts at $2C if none is running, and a message shows: RACE LOST when the lamp says the opponent finished first (and $C362 is set to $80), RACE WON in a league race, LAPS OVER in practice. Then copies $C395 into bit 6 of $C362.
Moves the text cursor to column X, row Y: prints code $1F and the two.
Draws the player's clock (0) in the dashboard's third place, with its hundredths only while $82 says a lap's time is showing. X is kept.
Prints the digit in A (adds $30, '0').
Sets clock X to 0:00.00.
Moves clock X on by 0.14 seconds, the length of a pass of the race (seven frames of the 50 a second): the race is timed by its passes, not by the clock on the wall.

Adds A hundredths to clock X in decimal mode; past 59 seconds the minutes go up, to 9 at most. The player's clock is drawn each time it carries into the seconds, unless a lap's time is showing or no lap has started.

After a bump ($C352): the crack across the top of the frame is drawn to the mean of the three points' damage ($C3CB, from $C3C3-$C3C5, with $1B88). A bump of 20 or more ($C35C) also takes one from $C719, a count the player keeps from race to race (10 at the start of a season), drawn with $F021 and $F673 for 64 passes ($C302, then $F668), with sound effect 1; a smaller bump makes sound effect 4.
The best lap's lamp: colour 11 while the best is the opponent's ($C395), 7 otherwise.
Sets the colour RAM of the lamp at $DBDA-$DBDB to Y.
The lamp for who leads: colour 11 when $F5E9 comes back with N clear, which LAPS_DONE takes as the opponent ahead, 7 otherwise; Y comes back with it.
Sets the colour RAM of the lamp at $DBCC-$DBCD to Y.

Every fourth pass: the sixteen bits at $39/$3A times 5/16, drawn as four digits (thousands, hundreds, tens and units) into the dashboard's sprites, after a blank, or a minus while $C36A bit 7 is set. Taking 100 off with a borrow from the high byte takes 101 by mistake, as the carry is clear there.
The speed bar's length from the speed along the road ($0159): twice its excess over 17, plus one, times $B7/256, drawn with command $43; 0 below 17 or from $91.

Draws clock Y in place X of the dashboard (the sprite rows at $1296) as M:SS.HH: the minutes, the colon, the seconds, the point and the hundredths, which are blank unless A has bit 7 set. $6F records which sprites changed.
Where each of the dashboard's four times starts in the sprite data from $4000.
Draws the L (laps) and the B on the dashboard.

Puts a message into the two sprites at $7F80 and $7FC0, from the table at $1329: Y is its first byte and A its number of groups, each a place in the sprites and three characters. A '<' moves the whole line half a character (four pixels) left. The glyphs' rows 1-6 are taken from the font. $C355 says a message is up. X is kept.
The table offset of the message showing.
Its number of groups.

The cockpit messages: WRECK, RACE WON, RACE LOST, DROP START, PRESS FIRE, PAUSED, LAPS OVER, DEFINE KEYS, STEER LEFT, STEER RIGHT, AHEAD +BOOST, BACK +BOOST, BACK, VERIFY KEYS, FAULT FOUND; each in groups of a sprite offset and three characters.
Sprite 0's place across in the dashboard's band, where IRQ_DASHBOARD puts it: the clocks' first block.
Sprite 1's place across in the dashboard's band.
Sprite 2's place across in the dashboard's band.
Sprite 3's place across in the dashboard's band.
The two dots between minutes and seconds: bit 7 set in the bytes 6 and 15 before X, rows 1 and 4 of the time.
Draws digit A into the sprite bytes from X, a pixel to the left. These four entries share the code at $1430: each takes rows 1-6 of the glyph and goes down a sprite row (three bytes) for each.

Draws digit A from X two pixels to the right: the glyph's bit 1 spills into bit 7 of the next byte, which is overwritten, and its bit 0, blank in every digit, is lost; the byte at X keeps its own bit 7.
Draws digit A from X a pixel to the right, keeping each byte's bit 7.
Draws digit A into the sprite bytes from X as it is. A digit $F0 draws a space and $FD a minus.
Points $1E at the glyph of character A plus $30 (its low seven bits) in the font at $7FC0, eight bytes a character, and sets Y to 1.
Places, points and colours sprites 2-7 for the dashboard (the clocks, the messages and the front wheels), with the sprites' shared colours black and white, and turns them on ($6E keeps which are on).
DASH_SPRITES reads its pointers from $14B6 + X for X from 7 down to 2, so its table starts two bytes on, at $14B8. Here: the high byte of STA $D015 and the RTS.
Sprites 2-7's pointers, $64, $63, $69, $67, $68 and $60. DASH_SPRITES reads each of these four tables from two bytes before it, plus the sprite's number.
Sprites 6 and 7's pointers, $68 and $60, the end of dash_sprite_pointers. DASH_SPRITES reads the colours from $14BC + X.
Sprites 2-7's colours: cyan for 2 and 3, grey for the front wheels, 4 and 5 the left and 6 and 7 the right (each wheel a sprite above another).
Sprites 6 and 7's colours, grey. DASH_SPRITES reads the places across from $14C2 + X.
Sprites 2-7's places across.
Sprites 6 and 7's places across. DASH_SPRITES reads the places down from $14C8 + X.
Sprites 2-7's places down.

Moves the two front wheels' sprites up and down with the first two points' springs ($83/$86), through the sine table at $A700, from the height $1C; a wheel that would sit too low has its sprite turned off and its top drawn into the bitmap (command $40) instead, and one coming back up has the bitmap's drawing put back to its rest.
Draws a wheel's top at height A (command $40).
The car is wrecked: unless the countdown is running it drops ($0E = 2, $1C = $92, $3C = $82), the countdown starts at $3C and WRECK shows.

While $C9 is set: a swerve of sixteen passes ($C30F) steers by the wave at $1601 ($C30D one way, $C30E the other, $C357 the throttle). A new one starts at random, the more often the higher $C773, when $C353 allows it and $0710 for piece $C375 does not forbid it.
Sixteen steps of a wave, signed, for SWERVE.
Clears the league's points ($C728-$C763) and $C77F, puts the twelve drivers back in order at $C758 and sets each one's count at $83B0 back to 10.
Keeps the random numbers' state ($02-$06) at $1648.
Sets the random numbers' state ($02-$06) from the five bytes ending at $1643 plus Y: Y = 4 the fixed seed at $1643, Y = 9 those SAVE_RANDOM kept.
The random numbers' first state, which LOAD_RANDOM puts at $02-$06 with Y = 4.
Where SAVE_RANDOM keeps the state.

Starts a frame's view: each column's top and bottom limits ($C640/$C680) from those kept at $C280/$C2C0, the edges at $0280/$02C0 cleared, the view cleared with the bonnet put back (CMD_CLEAR_VIEW), $F1DC, and the flags $C3A9, $C3DA, $6D and $C303 cleared.

Draws a frame's view of the track. From the piece the car is over ($FF6A, or $F117 from $AF and $B1, into $2E and $C374) it draws the pieces ahead, each with DRAW_PIECE, POINTS_TO_LINES and NEXT_PIECE. It starts from the car's piece, or from the one after it when the eye is already past that piece's end ($8E = $80, PLACE_ALONG); while the eye is in its piece's first segment ($8E = 0) the opponent is drawn first if it is on the piece before ($A6, OPP_DRAW_HERE). It draws two pieces, then two more: five more while the car is lowered at the start ($2F), and on Draw Bridge (track 5) one more for each piece the car is short of piece $31 when that is two or fewer. When no piece is under the car it is off the track and wrecked ($6B = $C0). In a league race the opponent moves (OPPONENT_MOVE) and its car is placed among the pieces. Then the view's column limits, the fills, and the sky above the track (CMD_FILL_ABOVE).

Draws piece $2E: its place and shape ($F02F, $F0C5, PIECE_POINTS), then which way it is seen ($C3A8: bit 7 when it is behind the eye, bit 6 when seen from its far end); each of its points, near to far or far to near as it is seen, is turned into the eye's frame ($A026), projected (PROJECT_X, PROJECT_Y) and checked against the last point on its side (OVERLAP); points before $27 are left out. Last, every point in sight is turned by the roll ($280E).

Point X against the last point drawn on its side of the road ($CC for the left, $CD for the right): when it lies further out across the screen, the road's edge folds back over itself there, so the point is marked ($A350 = 2) and a copy of it made (point X plus $20, at $A220/$A2B8), projected and turned, to close the edge.

The last two points of the piece just drawn become the first two of the next (all six of their tables), and $CC/$CD start again from them; after a piece behind the eye ($C3A9) the next starts from scratch ($D0 = 0).

Puts the piece's points into the tables, in pairs across the road, from its shape's two lists ($98 for the left edge, $CA for the right): a point's height is in the high three bits of its byte (shifted left once) and its distance along in the low four, or in two bytes each when $A2 bit 7 is set; each is added to the piece's place ($3F/$35, $40/$36) into $8040 and $A330. Points past the distance $19 (from $2A less $D3, how far the view reaches) are left out ($A330 = $80). $8080 records the start line's piece ($C766) and the points whose first byte has bit 7 set, which get a line across the road.

Joins the piece's points with lines, pair by pair: each point to the last one on its side of the road (ALONG_SIDE) and to its copy where the edge folds back (TO_COPY), the near or far line first as the car is rolled ($C3DC, $0126). The colour of each side alternates by pair ($FC01, from $C6 and $D8), the same from the 40th pair on; a pair marked at $8080 gets a line across the road, in the colour its low two bits pick (LINE_COLOUR), its ends first moved by ACROSS_LINE_ENDS. The opponent's car is drawn when its pair is reached ($E195, $E1B1).
The line from point $C6 to the last point drawn on its side ($CC or $CD, as $A0 says), by $FE91.
The line from point $C6 to its copy, point $C6 plus $20, by $FE91.

Each of the first two points of the piece that lies inside the view's columns but in front of the screen ($A2E4, $A24C) is moved along its edge towards the point before it ($8D, from $E808 and $E631), so that the line to it can be drawn; then re-projected ($E641).

Grows the crack across the top of the windscreen to match the damage: while its length $25 is below $C3CB, one more pixel pair. Each step wanders up or down a row at random (rows 3-5 of the bitmap's top line, kept at $1C15) and cuts a notch three rows deep into the frame at $6026. A step into a gap already open adds one to the damage instead (SET_DAMAGE). When the crack reaches the far side ($78), or the damage reaches $80, the car is wrecked.
Sets each point's damage ($C3C3-$C3C5) to twice the mean ($C3CB).
The row the crack is on (3 to 5).
The masks that keep the other three pixel pairs of a byte.
The masks of the four pixel pairs of a byte.
Runs command $3F, the crane's chains.
Clears the menus' panel in the bitmap at $4000: sixteen character rows of 28 characters from $4B60.
Sets up the top of the menus' screen: eight rows filled (command $55), a line of $AA across row $5F from column $38 (HLINE_SCREEN), and the title picture unpacked (command $32, UNPACK_TITLE).

Reads the joystick ($F79E, into $66: bit 0 forward, 1 back, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire). Left and right steer ($C5 = $F1 or $0F) while a spring is pressed. Fire is the boost ($C398 is 0 while it is held). Forward drives ($0150/$0151 from $C384/$C385) and the engine keeps driving after it is let go ($C39B bit 7); back brakes ($0150/$0151 = $FF10) and stops the drive. No drive while the car is lowered or dropped, or past $78 along the road. Then $F60F.

With $C359 set, in place of the view's column limits: a line across the whole view (points 2 and 3, from -376 to 632) at the horizon's height for the pitch ($33/$69), in colour $2C, then back to $3D. $C365 keeps the roll's sign ($0124) meanwhile.
Runs command $3C, the moving bridge, on Draw Bridge (track 5) only.

Where across the road the opponent aims ($2C, from its place $B0; the player's is $2B). Close behind the player ($39/$3A, the distance between the cars, and less than $32 apart across) it may bump ($209C, OPP_BUMP); within $18 it goes round (LINE_ROUND), unless its driver's flags at $AEE0 (bit 3) say to keep its line; nearer than $32 it holds the player's line (bit 1, LINE_HOLD) or passes (LINE_PASS), as it does within $C8 for a driver with bit 5, and always once it is ahead ($C36A bit 7). Otherwise its own line: $40 or $6E across (bit 3), mirrored for the odd-numbered drivers ($C773), or the middle when either of the next two pieces says so ($B240). Then it steers towards that line by ten a pass ($C357 can push it either way) while a wheel is on the road ($C9), keeping between $20 and $E0. $C308 is set while the cars are within $40 and either the opponent is ahead or they are in line; then the car in front has less drag.
Aims $20 or $E0 across, away from the side the player is on ($77), when the cars are within $38 across.

Passes the player when the cars are within $38 across ($51): the opponent aims for the edge on its own side, $20 when it is below the player across ($77 bit 7) and $E0 when above, unless the player is near that edge (below $60, or from $A0), when it aims for the other. Further apart it keeps the place it is at ($B0, set by OPPONENT_LINE).
Aims at the player's line ($2B).
The first piece, from the player's ($C374) on round the track, whose number at $044E is X; $FF when there is none. X is kept.
Where PIECE_FROM_HERE keeps X.

Moves the opponent's car, while it races ($C37C): its piece's place ($F02F), its wheels (OPP_WHEELS), a swerve now and then (SWERVE), its engine and grip (OPP_ENGINE, OPP_GRIP) and its speed (OPP_SPEED); then along the road by its speed ($D6/$D7) times $BD, in $A1/$23/$C4, on to the next piece ($C375) as $C4 passes the piece's length $BE.
Lowers the opponent's car onto the track ($E4DA) from a height above the road of $68 to $E7, at random, for each of its wheels.

Picks the opponent's limits for the race at random, from ranges for its track (the second set while $C71A is set): the top speed at $2099 ($BFAA/$BFB2), $209A ($BFBA/$BFC2) and $209B ($C774 or $C775). It runs RANDOM 256 times first. Nothing while $31A1 and $C77F are both set.

The opponent's speed $D6/$D7: plus the engine's push ($C3B6/$C3B7, less its speed again and $23 more on a climb, $B2), less a drag of its speed squared over 64 (its speed taken 20 lower while it is in front and close, $C308), plus, while a wheel is on the road, the slope's pull from the heights of its front and back wheels ($07EC-$07F2); never below 0.
The tail of OPP_SPEED: A:$14 added to the speed $D6/$D7.
The opponent's engine: $C3B6/$C3B7 from $C386/$C387, 25 less during a swerve ($C30F), none while no wheel is on the road ($C9).

The piece's speed limit ($0710, or the opponent's own at $2099 when that is lower and the piece's has no bit 7) against the opponent's speed $D7: over it, the engine's push is reversed ($C3C7 set); far over it, or under it, the push is doubled, except just under a limit it has reached.
The opponent's top speed for the race, from OPP_PICK.
A second limit for the race, from OPP_PICK.
From OPP_PICK, the track's $C774, or $C775 in the Super League (3 to 10): WHEELS_ON_ROAD adds damage for a spring pressed past its line only while its count $E1 is below it.

The cars meet, while the opponent races ($C37C). Unless the opponent has a wheel on the road ($C9) and the player's springs press ($6A), the heights are tested first: the player's ($46/$64) less the opponent's wheel 0, at the front ($07CC/$07D0), plus $28, must be within $C0 either way, or it returns at once with $C369 set to 3. When they are and $C369 is not 0, it counts $C369 down and pushes the player's car in height ($0180/$0183), harder the nearer the heights, by their difference's sign: at most three times after a pass at heights too far apart, since OPPONENT_LINE clears $C369 while the cars are apart. Close beside ($51 below $2D, $39 below 8) it pushes sideways, 8 or $F8 by which side the opponent is on ($77, into $0182). Once a bump ($E0, cleared by OPPONENT_LINE) it pushes along by half the difference of their speeds plus 3 in its direction ($0181/$0184). $C371 is set, the pushes' high bytes plus 2 are added to each point's damage ($C3C3-$C3C5, held at $FF) and $C352 is set.

Takes in a bump's pushes ($C371): the opponent's speed less the push along (never below 0), its wheels' speeds less the push up over 16, the player's springs' forces ($0170-$0175) plus the pushes, which are then cleared; sound effect 2.

The opponent's three wheels as springs: each one's height ($07CC/$07D0) against the road's under it ($07EC/$07F0) and the spring's length ($28, or $7C on a piece with $B2 bit 7), at most $60 below; the spring's push ($07C4/$07C8, up to $3FF), and $C9 non-zero while any wheel is on the road. Each wheel's speed ($07E4/$07E8) is a share of the three pushes and its own, over 8. A driver with bit 2 of its flags now and then (one pass in 16) bounces its back wheel ($07DE = $A0) when all are nearly still. The speeds are added into the heights (half of them), the wheels kept together (OPP_SPREAD), and the opponent's model's points placed ($8040/$A330, points $3C-$3F).
Which of the model's points ($3C-$3F) each wheel sets.
The difference of the heights of wheels X and Y: its size in A:$14, its sign in bit 7 of $17.

Keeps wheels X and Y within A:$51 of each other in height: the higher is lowered to it and their speeds averaged (all three's when Y is 2). With Y = 2 and no wheel on the road, when wheel X rises no faster than the back wheel by $10, the car is tilted: the front wheels' speeds up by 4 and the back's down by 4.
The tilt OPP_SPREAD gives the three wheels' speeds, low bytes.
High bytes.
Sets the speeds of wheels X and Y ($07DC/$07E0) both to their mean.

Point X's place across the screen ($A200/$A298) from its distance across ($78:$52) and its depth ($77:$51), through PROJECT_LOG; a point on the left (a negative distance) is moved two pixels further out. While the menus draw the track's picture ($F3C1) the game rewrites these first three bytes to a JMP to PROJECT_X_PAIR.
PROJECT_X with the distance's low byte in A.

Divides by logarithms. The distance across, made eight bits with a count of the shifts it took, gives its logarithm ($AA00 low, $AB00 high, plus $A610 for the shifts) in $70/$71; the depth's the same way in $A9/$AA. Their difference, turned back by EXP, is the point's offset from the middle of the screen ($A7/$A8, or $32/$3E on the other side), into $A200/$A298 for point $16. $AB/$AC keep the depth's logarithm less the result's, plus $20, for PROJECT_Y. The branch at $24F8 is rewritten by PROJECT_X ($90, BCC, or $B0, BCS) to swap the sides for a negative distance.

The branch PROJECT_X_AT rewrites: BCC ($90) as loaded, BCS ($B0) while the distance across is negative, so one body serves both sides of the screen. From here the four endings, by the signs of the depth's and the distance's logarithms' difference.

Point X's height on the screen ($A24C/$A2E4): its height ($8040/$A330) less the eye's ($37/$38), by its logarithm less $AB/$AC, turned back by EXP, from the horizon's line ($33/$69). The 8 taken off the logarithm is the operand at $262B, which the menus' picture of the track sets to $0B.
The operand of SBC #: 8 taken off the height's logarithm in a race, $0B while TRACK_PREVIEW draws the map, which flattens the heights. From here the height's row above or below the horizon.

The antilogarithm of A:$14 (from $E0:00 up; below that it gives $FF for 0 and 0 for anything else): its top bits pick an entry in the tables at $A800, $A880 and $A900, and the fractions at $AC00, $AC80 and $AD00 decide the rounding.

When the roll ($0126, with the top two bits of $0123) has changed: its sine and cosine from the quarter-wave table at $A700. $0300-$037F become the running sums of the sine (the high byte of $80 plus n times it), $0380-$03FF those of twice the cosine; $C328/$C334 half of $0100 plus n times the sine, and $C310/$C31C n times the cosine, for n from 1 to 8. The loops rewrite their own operands ($277B, $2781, $27A6, $27AD, $27B8, $27BE).
ROLL_TABLES writes the sine here, the ADC's operand, before the loop that sums it into $0300-$037F.
The low byte of the STY's address, stepped by INC from $00 to $7F: each running sum of the sine goes one byte further into $0300.
Twice the cosine's low byte, the ADC's operand, while twice the cosine is 256 or more: this loop adds one more to Y each step.
The low byte of this loop's STY $0380, stepped from $80 by INC until it wraps.
The cosine, then doubled in place by ASL: the ADC's operand for twice the cosine when it is under 256.
The low byte of the other loop's STY $0380, stepped from $80 until it wraps.
The roll the tables were last built for.
Its top two low bits.
The RTS ROLL_POINT branches to for a point out of sight.
Turns point X on the screen by the roll, about the middle ($80, $80), unless it is out of sight ($A330 bit 7).
Turns point X by the roll. A point near the middle (both high bytes 0) is turned with the tables of running sums at $0280-$03FF alone, when that does not overflow; any other by ROLL_FAR.
Turns point X by the roll with the products of its distances from the middle and the roll's sine and cosine: the whole eighths from $C310-$C33F and the rest from $0300-$03FF.

The game's random numbers: moves the forty-bit shift register at $02-$06 on by eight bits, mixing its fourth and fifth bytes back in, and gives its new first byte in A ($53 and $54 are its scratch). X and Y are kept.

Draws a piece of the wreck, X the speck, at column $80A0 and row $C260 of speck $C6: lines joined end to end ($FEC9), their steps from the tables at $2A3E (across) and $2A4D (down), ten lines for an odd X and five for an even one; bit 1 of X picks the colour ($FC01).
Where each shape's steps start in the tables.
Each shape's number of lines, less one.
Each shape's first column, added to the speck's.
The lines' steps across.
The lines' steps down.

Where a piece of the wreck, X, starts: the first column out from the middle ($40), right then left, where the outline of the view's top ($C640) steps by 4 or more, a few pixels about it at random. $C260 = $D2 (none) when there is no such column.

A save while $C77B is set, a load otherwise. For a save, the message to ready the tape or disc and a press of fire. The name typed (NAME_ENTRY_AT, into $AEC1) and checked (FILE_NAME_CHECK, again until it suits; the C= key leaves). Then the random numbers kept (SAVE_RANDOM), the border red, the Hall of Fame's or a game for several's file made ready (FILE_BUFFER), the screen at $0400 filled with spaces, and with the KERNAL banked in ($01 $36): IOINIT, RAMTAS, the KERNAL's vectors from $0800, CINT, the border green, the KERNAL's messages on, and the drive set going (command $47 with X 0).
The screen at $0400 to spaces: the KERNAL's screen while the file is saved or loaded.
$A000 kept around the KERNAL's routines.
SETMSG ($FF90 with the KERNAL in; the game's LOAD_14 sits under it): the KERNAL's messages on.
The file on device 1 (tape) or 8 (disc) by $0840 ($2C21).
A directory is the name "$" ($94D6), loaded to $4000.
Otherwise the old file is scratched from the disc (command $47 with X $80), and the name is the twelve letters at $AEC1.
A save: the league's 192 bytes at $8000-$80BF, or for the Hall of Fame and a game for several ($C367) $4000-$41FF or $4000-$40FF; a load to $8000, or $4000 for those.
The KERNAL's carry, and its status ($90) but for the end of the file (bit 6), into $C301 bit 7; on a failure the drive is set going again.
$A000 put back, a pause, and the ROMs out ($01 $35); a failure into $C39A ($80); a directory shown (DIRECTORY_SCREEN).
The game's screen and interrupt back, the file read in where it goes (FILE_BUFFER) and the random numbers put back (LOAD_RANDOM), since RAMTAS has cleared the zero page.
The device for each answer to "disk or tape" ($0840): 1, the tape, or 8, the disk.
Runs command $45, the view cleared, with $3DF8 as its flags.
Runs command $3E, the fill above the edges.
Runs command $46, the view's colour RAM brought up to date.
Runs command $41.
Runs command $42, while $6D bit 7 says there are spans to fill.
Runs command $3D, the view's column limits, or HORIZON while $C359 is set.
Sixteen pieces fly while the car is wrecked, with a stones' sound of $0A and the car's speed ($0188), 16 at most.
All 32 specks of dust gone ($C260 = $D4).

The dust thrown up from the road while the car is on it ($C30A, or lowered at the start, $0E), not wrecked and moving ($0188): 32 specks, with the sound of the stones (sound effect 1, its pitch at $AF8C from the speed, 50 at most, or now and then 3 or $0D).

With A the sound's pitch less 2 and X the last speck. In the air ($6A 0) all go (DUST_CLEAR). On the road each speck is rubbed out where it was and moved (DUST_PLOT): it falls faster by 2 a pass ($4120) and moves across by $4100. One that has gone below the view starts again at random on the road's edge ($C280; for a wreck, DEBRIS_START), going up by a quarter of $C350 and a little more, and out from the middle by an eighth of its distance from it.

Draws speck X: two pixels, one above the other, cleared with the masks at $A4C0, at its column ($80A0) and row ($C260); for a wreck, a piece of debris (DEBRIS). A speck outside the view (rows $41 to $B7, columns below $80) is gone ($D2), and Z clear says so.
Points $1E at the byte of the bitmap being drawn ($12) that holds pixel column X of row Y, less Y, and reads it.

The size of the speed along the road ($0159/$0156) into $0188, and the engine's note from it ($5D, which the interrupt adds into $5F each frame, clicking the engine at each carry): eight times the speed below 8, twice it plus $30 from there, $FF at most. In the air the note falls by a quarter each pass.

The turn on the car. Its heading against the road's under it: the piece's direction ($0189/$018A, flipped by $A4) less the car's ($0122/$0125), with a quarter turn either way on a piece with $B2 bit 7 ($2EFD/$2F00); its size in $7F:$7D. Steering ($C5) turns the car by the speed along the road ($0159) times $C8 (more, or less, on such a piece, by the side of its turn, $9D), plus the difference over 16 when it steers towards the road's direction. Without steering the car is turned towards the road's direction, by the difference times the speed plus 10, over 128, at least 1. More than $1E off, it is turned back at once by the excess. The turning force $0119/$011F is the steering's less the car's spin about that axis ($010D/$0113), 0 in the air ($6A). The next piece is taken when the car is within 2 of the piece's end ($BE, $C3).
The quarter turns STEERING adds on a piece with $B2 bit 7, low bytes.
The quarter turns' high bytes.

Draws the windscreen's frame into the bitmap at $4000 from the picture at $6000: the edges above and below the view (patterns of 24 bytes repeated across, from $6130, $6270, $63B0 and $64F0), the two pillars (FRAME_PILLAR), and the corners.
A pillar of the frame: eighteen character rows of 16 bytes into the bitmap from ($1E), A its high byte, from the three rows at X:Y and below in turn, then the corners' bytes.

The track's name in a box under the view: printed half a row down from column $301B (by track, so that it sits in the middle), then four lines across ($3017's rows, 20 bytes from column $58) and two up, the left in bits 0-1 and the right in bits 6-7, 20 rows from row $E9.
The rows of the title box's four lines across.
For each track, the column TRACK_TITLE prints "The " from ($3460), so that it and the track's name, four columns on, sit in the middle.
The loop of PRINT_STRING.
Prints string X of the table at $3407, up to its $FF.
The track of slot A in the league's order: its number into $C77D from $3728, and its colour into $C76B from $3730, the pair's other one in the Super League ($C71A).
Twelve colours from $C6C0 into colour RAM at $DAB6.

The game's first menu ($31A0 set meanwhile): a single player's league, or a game for several, whose drivers' names are entered one by one ($ED7F) until the menu ($EE36) says no more or there are eight. $31A1 is the number of players less one.

The table of a game for several. After a round ($C39C and $31A5 set, ROUND_RESULTS): the track bonus points, the track's name, $91CF's points and the race times. After one race: the race's results, and "Track record" when $C74B is 7 or more. Then a row of TABLE_ROW for each driver from $50 to $8A.
At column 6 of row Y, the menus' string $93 ("Track:") and the track's name; for several players in the Super League, string $63 after it.
The row MULTI_RESULTS starts its table on, by the number of players.
The panel line, by the number of players.
Bit 7 while CHOOSE_PLAYERS runs: the panel is left without a heading, and PRINT_STRING_E000 prints from the menus' table.
The number of players less one; 0 is the single player's league.
Whose turn it is in a game for several.
The number of races in a season: 6, or for several players their number.
The player's driver, $0B.
Bit 7 while MULTI_RESULTS is to show the bonus points.
The race of the season, from 0.
The division chosen for practice, 3 less the line taken (PRACTICE_TRACK), which the list of its tracks is drawn from.
Set after a practice race, so that PRACTICE_TRACK skips the choice of division once; it clears it with LSR.
NEW_DRIVERS' count of the pool, 0 to 2.

The menus' strings, each to $FF: "SELECT", "Single Player League", "Multiplayer", "Enter another driver", "Continue", "Tracks in DIVISION ", the drivers' heading "DRIVER BEST-LAP RACE-TIME", "Track:", "DRIVERS CHAMPIONSHIP" and "Track record", among others; $1F col row moves the cursor.

The row of the heading "DRIVER      BEST-LAP RACE-TIME", which MULTI_RESULTS sets before it prints it. Then the strings "Track:  The ", "DRIVERS CHAMPIONSHIP" and "Track record" (each with its place), and a line of twelve dashes.
Twelve dashes, a blank time.
Twelve dashes, then "New track record".
The loop of PRINT_STRING_B.
Prints string X of the table at $32AD, up to its $FF.
"TRACK BONUS POINTS", "FINAL SEASON", "Race Time: ", "Best Lap : ", "HALL of FAME", "SUPER LEAGUE" and "TRACK DRIVER LAP-TIME DRIVER RACE-TIME".
Two spaces, then NUMBER_SP.
A in decimal: one digit below 10, two from 10.
A in decimal in two places: a space before a single digit.
Prints the two decimal digits of A.
Adds race time X to race time Y, in decimal: hundredths at $8298, seconds at $82B0 (sixty to the minute, the excess carried) and minutes at $8398.

A new league. For several players, two opponents taken from the pool under the chips: names from $DC00 (16 bytes each) to $AE00 and their driving from $DCE0 to $AEE0, by division ($E8E1), one of three at random in the Super League ($C718 set). $31A3 is the number of races in a season: 6 for one player, the players' number for several. $31A6 starts at 0.
The raster interrupt off, interrupts off, and RAM under the chips ($01 = $34).
The chips back ($01 = $35), interrupts on, and the raster interrupt on.

The strings PRINT_STRING prints, each to $FF, $1F col row moving the cursor: "DIVISION " (its row at $3409), "RACE  " (row at $3416), "Track:  ", "The ", " V ", "steer to rotate view or fire to continue", "RESULT", "Race Winner: ", "Fastest Lap: ", "RESULTS TABLE" with its heading "DRIVER RACED WIN LAP PTS", "Promotion for ", "Relegation for ", " CHANGES", "NAME?", " 2pts", " 1pt" and " of ".
The row "DIVISION " is printed on.
The row "RACE  " is printed on.
The column of string $58, "The " under the view, from $301B by track; the track's name follows it four columns on.
BLANK_SCREEN, in a border of $3FBA's colour.
The menus' screen behind the panel: blanked with a black border, the title (MENU_TITLE), high resolution, the wooden posts (WOOD_POSTS), the division's panel (DIVISION_PANEL), and the screen on.

The panel cleared and coloured (PANEL_FRAME), its heading rows lit, and its heading: the division ($C718, into $C360) for one player, or the menus' string $A0 for several. Nothing more while players are being chosen.
At row Y, "DIVISION " and its number (4 less $C360); in the Super League, the string at $E0BB, whose row is $E0BD.
NEXT_RACE after the race ($C372 set): the winner and the fastest lap.

The panel before a race: the division, the race's track (slot $C77F of the division's pair, or the player's turn for several), "RACE n of m", the two drivers ($C771 V $C772) and their records ($9319, $9225); after a race ($C372 set), "RESULT", the winner ($C76F) and the fastest lap ($C770), with their points. Then WAIT_FIRE.
WAIT_FIRE, then TEXT_ON_ROWS.
Text on the character rows again (command $20 with X = 0).
The division's table: the drivers from $50 to $8A, by place, each a row of TABLE_ROW under "RESULTS TABLE", or MULTI_RESULTS for several players. Then WAIT_FIRE.

The row of the table's driver $C7 (the driver at that place, $C758): the name, then the races ($C740), the wins ($C728), the fastest laps ($C734) and the points ($C74C); for several after a round ($C39C), the two race times ($99FF). Z is set at the table's end ($8A).
Waits for fire to be let go, a moment (DELAY 5), then for fire.
To RESULTS_TABLE for several players.

The whole league: the four divisions, the top first ($C360 3 to 0), each with its heading, its two tracks (half a row down) and its three drivers, from $C70C. Then WAIT_FIRE. For several players, RESULTS_TABLE.
The tracks in the league's order, two to a division, the bottom division first.
The colour of each slot's track.
At panel line A, the race's two drivers ($C771 and $C772, from $E8E5), " V " between.
The division's panel and the season's changes (CHANGES), then WAIT_FIRE.

The end of a season. The league's order from the tables ($C758 into $C70C) and " CHANGES" for division $C360: its winner promoted ("Promotion for ") and its last relegated ("Relegation for ", none from the bottom division). From the top division only the player goes up, "to the SUPER LEAGUE" ($E0A7), or with "EXCELLENT DRIVING - WELL DONE" ($E0CE) in it, and then no relegation line is printed; when another driver wins it, only the relegation is. Then each pair at the divisions' edges swapped in the order. A player who won the top division outside the Super League goes into it ($C71A set), where the order starts again at 0-11 and $C718 is 0; otherwise $C718 is the division of the player's new place ($381D, 0 the bottom). $C719, the car's whole parts, is set back to 10 when the player won the top division or is in the bottom one; elsewhere the damage carries into the next season.
The division of each place in the league, three to a division.
X is the place of driver A in the league's order ($C70C), $FF when it is not there.
Not read.
The panel's lines' first rows, by line number ($19).
The last row of the table MULTI_RESULTS draws.
Row Y of the panel lit (the colours at $3944 + $0E, whose colour is $3953).
LINES with 3.
LINES with 2.
A rows of the panel lit from line $19's first row ($3837), a line across above them and, unless $C356 is set, under them; then NEXT_LINE.
The cursor to column 5 of row $7A, line $19 on, and the text half a row down.
Text printed half a row (four pixels) down (command $20 with X = $80).
Prints driver X's name, thirteen characters from $AE00 + 16 X.
Prints track X's name, fifteen characters from $AF00 + 16 X.
Points $1E at the name and prints $14 characters of it.
A byte with one bit clear, for each bit.
A byte with one bit set, for each bit.
The colours of the panel, character rows 8 to 25 of the screen at $7C00: its frame, and inside, the top eight rows in one colour and the rest in another.
Points $1E at row Y of the screen at $7C00 (40 bytes a row) and puts X, the column, in Y.
A rows of runs from the table at $3944 + X (each a count, then the colour), back to back from $1E + Y.
Copies the bytes from $397A + X (a count, then the bytes) to $1E + Y.
The panel's colour runs, a count and a colour each.
The colour of a lit row of the panel, which the menus change.
The panel frame's colour bytes, a count first.

The grain of a wooden post at column X: eight passes, one for each bit of $17, from row $F7 up to $70, in runs of 4 to 11 rows at random, each either $18's bits set or $17's and $18's set with $19's kept.
Points $1E at the byte of the bitmap at $4000 that holds multicolour column X (four to a byte, $40 the left of the view) of row Y, less Y, from the row tables at $A500 and $A600.

The ten wooden posts either side of the panel, at the columns at $3A1E, their grain drawn by WOOD_GRAIN from the same random numbers every time (the fixed seed, the race's own put back after), and the line across their tops at row $70.
The posts' columns.
The bits WOOD_GRAIN keeps of each post.
The bits WOOD_GRAIN sets for each post.
A bytes of $AA across row Y from column X.
A line across the panel, under row $74.
$1C bytes of $FF across row Y from column $40.
A bytes of $FF across row Y from column X, every fourth column.
$15's bits set in A rows up from row Y, at column X.

The race screen's colours into the screen at $7C00, from the runs at $3AD9: a count below $C8 and its byte; $C8 + n, n times the group of runs that follows, its number of runs first; $FF the end. The track's colour ($C76B) goes into two of them first, and $7C53 and $7C74 get $0E after.
Run X of $3AD9: the count, then the byte, stored across pages.
The race screen's colour runs.
The track's colour, put here by RACE_SCREEN_COLOURS.
And here.

The game, and where it starts again. The drivers' names and driving copied from the pool under the chips ($DC00) to $AE00, $E85B, the screen with the panel, the players chosen and the league shown. Then for good: the main menu ($EF3A), and a practice race ($C76C clear: RACE_SETUP, RACE) or the league.
A key held at the panel before a race ($20) skips the race: $C304 and $C362 set.
The league: new drivers, then a season.
A season: the clocks cleared (the first sixteen at 9 minutes), $C76D and $C76E cleared.

A race of the season: the pairing ($E8E5). When the player is one of the two ($31A4), the opponent into $C773, the panel (NEXT_RACE), the track (RACE_SETUP) and the race (RACE), $9846 on either side, $9319 and $E87F after, then the panel again with the results (RACE_DONE, RESULTS_TABLE). Otherwise the race is worked out ($E87F).
The next race; at the season's end the changes and the league for one player, or the next player's turn for several.

Before a race, the track from above: a grey border, the race's state cleared (CLEAR_RACE), the view's rows all of colour 8, the menus' screen in the track's colours (command 3), the colours, the frame and the track's name, the track's pieces made ($EA34) and drawn ($F386), turned by left and right until fire is pressed (VIEW_KEYS). Then a black border.
"steer to rotate view or fire to continue" on the bottom row, its colour $3B.

A race. The race's screen put back (command $34 with X $80, SAVE_RESTORE_SCREEN) and cleared, the race's state cleared, multicolour, START_ORDER, then the opponent placed on the start piece ($C765 into $C375, 4 along at $C4, $4C across at $B0) and dropped onto the road (OPP_DROP). Then the car placed on piece X ($F488) and two steps drawn and shown before the screen goes on (one after a wreck, $3DF8 set), and the race's loop.
The car put on the road at piece X, after a wreck too.

The race's loop, once a pass: the controls, a step of the world, $E104, the view, the dust, the wheels, the crane's chains and the drawbridge, the speed bar, the damage, the clocks and the distance, the bitmap shown, and the pause.
The race is over ($C351, while the bitmap at $6000 is drawn, on the road or over the line): the lamp, message $3C, the engine quiet, and WAIT_FIRE.

Wrecked on the road ($6B bit 7, $6A): $C373 set from $6B when $64 is negative or below 2, and once $C368 runs out, with $6C clear, the sound effects stopped (STOP_EFFECTS) and the car put back on the road at piece $C309 (CAR_ON_ROAD), and the race goes on.
Off the road or the race lost: key $2F ends the race.

The end of the race: $C362 set unless $C364, a black border, the sprites off, the sound effects stopped (STOP_EFFECTS). In a league race ($C76C bit 7) for several players the player's $C719 is kept at $83B0 (and their clock cleared unless $C378 is 4); then $C719 back from $C37E, except in a league race for one player, where the race's damage stays. The random numbers kept, and the race's screen kept for the next race to put back (command $34 with X 0, SAVE_RESTORE_SCREEN).
Bit 7 once the race's screen is up; $40 while the track is seen from above, $41 at the panel.

A race's state cleared: $C300-$C3FF, $0774-$07FF, $4000-$40FF, the car's $0100-$018F and zero page from $02. Then the eleven bytes from $BFEA (one on in the Super League) to $C382; the view's rows' colours 7 to $17; the clocks; the roll's tables; the sound effects stopped (STOP_EFFECTS); the race's random numbers; the dashboard's labels and lamps; $C76A, the league's or the Super League's count from $C776 or $C777 in decimal; $C37E kept from $C719; and CLEAR_BARS.
$80 in the 32 bytes at $A350 and the 32 at $8080.
$C440-$C4C0, $80 in every eighth and 0 between, and $C43F $C0; for several players the player's $C719 from $83B0; then $F6A6.

While the bitmap at $6000 is being drawn ($C306 set), key $0D pauses the race: the sound effects stopped (STOP_EFFECTS), message $4C, $97AF until key $34, then the message that was showing back and the sounds started again (START_SOUNDS).
Sound effects 6 and 5, $E104, voices 1 and 3 started on the pulse wave ($41) and the volume up ($F5).

Asks the interrupt to show the bitmap just drawn: flips $C306, sets $12 to the bitmap to draw into next ($20 for the one at $6000, or $18 plus the $E8 at $A1F2, which comes to 0, for the one at $4000) and $C370 to match ($80 or 0), and sets $C37A for the interrupt, with interrupts off while it does.
Finishes a flip the interrupt has made ($C37B set), through FLIP_DONE; otherwise nothing.
Once the interrupt shows the new bitmap: the view's colour RAM brought up to date for it (command $46), two dashboard colours set, and $C37A and $C37B cleared.
Not called: the same as MENU_BITMAP with $D018 $78, and $C35F and $C370 0.
The menus' bitmap and screen shown: $D018 $70, $C35F and $C370 $80.
The screen on if it is off (with the raster interrupt's line, $32), and the raster interrupt enabled.
The screen on and the raster interrupt at line $32, whether it was off or not.
The border's colour while the screen is blanked.
BLANK_SCREEN with the border's colour in A.
Waits for the raster's first ten lines (giving up after 1,029 tries), then the border to $3FBA's colour, the screen blanked, and DELAY 1.
DELAY with 20.
Y times twenty times 256 turns of a loop, about two frames for each of Y.
DELAY's innermost loop. COLON reads from $3FF1 on, 15 bytes before the clock's sprite bytes at $4000: the colon's top dot.
DELAY's middle and outer loops. DRAW_TIME writes from $3FF6 on, ten bytes before the clock's sprite bytes.
DELAY's return. COLON's other dot is from $3FFA on, six bytes before the clock's sprite bytes.

Where the loader hands over (JMP $3FFB), run once: the screen blanked; the KERNAL's 32 bytes of vectors from $0314 kept at $0800 (VECTOR, the KERNAL still in); a pause of about 28,700 cycles; the screen back on, the ROMs out for good ($01 = $35), the NMI's vector to $9A32, every interrupt turned off, multicolour on and the sprites off; then the game's sum checked (CHECKSUM), multicolour bitmap mode (command 2), the SID's three voices stopped and its filter set, and the IRQ's vector to $CDAA.
The screen blanked. Once the start-up has run, $4000 is the clocks' sprites (DIGIT draws there, CLEAR_RACE clears $4000-$40FF) and the file that saves and loads are built in (FILE_BUFFER, SAVE_CODE).
X:Y set to $0800 and the carry set, for VECTOR. DIGIT writes from $4001 on, the byte a shifted digit spills into.
VECTOR (KERNAL $FF8D) copies the KERNAL's vectors from $0314 to $0800. FRAME_PILLAR writes from $4008 on, the left pillar's top.
The pause starts with A 0, so each turn of its inner loop is 256 SBCs. FILE_BUFFER's merge reads a loaded record's minutes from $400C on.
Sixteen turns of the pause's outer loop. The merge reads a loaded record's seconds from $400D on.
The outer loop's count. The merge reads a loaded record's hundredths from $400E on, and FRAME_PILLAR writes the pillar's corner there.
The pause's loops, then the screen on and the processor port's direction set. FRAME writes from $4010 on, the edge above the view from column 2.

The rest of the hand-over: the ROMs out, the NMI's vector to $9A32, every interrupt off, the video chip's modes, CHECKSUM, multicolour bitmap mode, the SID's voices stopped, the IRQ's vector to $CDAA, and the colour RAM filled from $5800. Prints the character in A into the bitmap at $4000, seven pixels wide, at column $85C5 (of 45) and row $85C6. $1F takes the next two bytes as the column and the row; 9 moves one column on; $7F moves back one and rubs out the character there; codes from $80 do nothing. The glyph is eight bytes at $7FC0 plus eight times the code. Its seven-pixel column is turned into a byte and a shift, and the glyph is shifted across the two bytes it straddles, kept from the pixels on either side by masks. With bit 7 of $85D0 set the character is drawn half a row lower, as the menus' highlighted lines are. The column moves on, back to 0 after 44.

The mask that keeps the pixels to the right of the glyph in its second byte.
The glyph's first byte column (eight pixels each).
How many pixels the glyph is shifted right within its first byte.
$40 while neither shift key is held, so WAIT_KEY reads the second half of its table.
