Tests one key, X its number in the keyboard matrix: bits 0-2 pick the line it drives low on CIA 1's port A ($DC00), bits 3-5 the bit it reads back on port B ($DC01). Gives X = $FF with N set when the key is held, X = 0 with Z set when not.
The eight single bits KEY_SCAN drives and reads, bit 0 to bit 7.

Waits for the last key it returned to be let go, then for any key, and gives that key's character in A from the table at $9125: the first half when a shift key is held, the second when not. The two shift keys themselves are skipped. X and Y are kept.

Starts a sound effect from the seven bytes at X (low) and Y (high): the slot (which voice), the control byte (its waveform), attack and decay, sustain and release, the pitch's high byte, the pulse width's high nibble, and how long the gate is held, in frames. The voice is silenced, set up and gated on; EFFECT_TICK lets it go.
The pulse width byte of the last effect started.
The slot of the last effect started.
Frames each slot's gate is still held; bit 7 set while it is being started.
Each slot's pitch, high byte.
Each slot's release time in frames, from its release nibble.
Frames left of each slot's release, before it is silenced.
Each slot's control byte with the gate bit cleared, written to let it go.
The SID register offset of each slot's voice: 0, 7 and 14.
The release times, in frames, for the sixteen values of the release nibble; roughly the SID's own release lengths, frame by frame.
Called by the interrupt every frame for slot 1, the second voice: counts down the frames its gate is held, then lets the gate go, then after its release time cuts the voice with CUT_EFFECT.
Stops the effect in slot X (command $15): its count is cleared and its voice's control and sustain-release registers set to 0.

The command dispatcher: A is the command, X (and Y) its argument. $01 shows the bitmap at $4000 in hi-res and $02 the one at $6000 in multicolour ($FE keeps which), $03 sets up the menus' screen, $10 copies or clears the view, $20 sets the half-row flag, $81 tests a key, $15 stops an effect, $32 unpacks the title picture (UNPACK_TITLE), $55 fills rows, $34 saves or restores what a menu covers, and $3C-$47 run the race's jobs: the drawbridge, the view's fills, the crane's chains, the front wheels, the speed bar, the opponent's table, the view cleared, the row colours and the disk's commands. Any other command does nothing.

Puts the menus' title picture together (the car on its ramp and the words STUNT CAR RACER) from the table the start-up left under the I/O area at $D400 (title_runs, loaded at $4F00): thirteen runs of bytes, each with its length and its destination in the first 39 bytes, copied into the bitmap at $4000; then 320 bytes for the screen at $7C00 and the 320 colour bytes, which go to colour RAM; and seventeen rows from $4A00 cleared. Interrupts from the video chip are off while the RAM under the I/O is in.

Command $34. With X below $80, as a race ends, keeps what the menus' bitmap at $4000 draws over, $57C0-$5FFF (sprite shapes and the race's screen at $5C00), in the race picture's view rows from $62A0 (eight rows of 256 bytes and a ninth of 64, a bitmap row of 320 apart), and colour RAM at $6DE0-$71DF. With X from $80, as a race starts, puts both back, and the dashboard from the copies under the chips: $D000-$D3FF to $7C00-$7FFF and $DD00-$DDFF to $7B00, with the RAM banked in and interrupts off.
Fills $52 rows of 320 bytes, from the address in X (low) and Y (high), with A.

The Draw Bridge's moving ends (command $3C, called on track 5 only). A count of passes at $C300 rises and falls over 32 passes; it rewrites the points of object $5F, the bridge's two ends, so that they rise and fall, and their heights at $0740-$0744. While either car is on pieces $33-$37, next to the bridge, it stays down ($E7 = 12).
Half the count in A picks a step from $8A0F; $0740, $0741 and $0742 become $C6 plus one, two and three steps.
The steps BRIDGE_HEIGHTS adds, for the sixteen positions of the bridge.
The heights $0743 and $0744 take, for the sixteen positions of the count.

Command $3D: for each of the view's 64 columns, keeps the lowest the top limit ($C680) and the bottom limit ($C640) have been: a height (256 less the sixteen bits at $69 and $33, 255 when those are 0 or less, 0 when they are past 256) less and plus that column's slope at $0380, mirrored when $0126 is negative.

Command $3E: in each of the view's 32 character columns (pixel columns $40-$BF, four to a byte), from the lowest of its four edges at $C600 upwards, each pixel above its own edge is set to colour 2. Once a row has all four, the rest of that character row is filled whole, and the character row is kept at $01C1 plus X (7 when the column never got that far), for SET_ROW_COLOURS.

Command $3F: the two chains the car hangs from before the start, drawn from row $C36B up to the top of the view at pixel columns $54 and $A8. While $2F is 0 their ends rise by a step that grows by 8 a pass ($C36C), until row $5F.
Draws one chain at pixel column X, upwards from row $C36B: links eight rows tall and two bytes wide, odd and even links taken in turn from the masks at $8BCD-$8C0C.
The masks that keep the background around a chain's links, left byte, for the sixteen rows of two links.
The masks that keep the background around a chain's links, right byte.
The chain's pixels, left byte, sixteen rows.
The chain's pixels, right byte.

Command $40: draws the top of a front wheel, X 0 the left and 1 the right, at the height in $14: eight rows taken from the tables at $8C70 (left) or $8C94 (right), starting further into them the lower the wheel, into both bitmaps. The wheels bounce with the suspension.
The left front wheel's top, three columns of bytes ($8C70, $8C78 and $8C80) read upwards from an offset set by the wheel's height.
FRONT_WHEEL's second column for the left wheel reads from here, eight bytes on along the same strip: one character row lower.
The third column, sixteen bytes on: the lowest row. From $8C88 the strip holds the wheel's edge, eleven bytes of $AC, $B0 and $C0, with zeros either side, so a wheel lower down shows less of it.
The right front wheel's top, three columns of bytes ($8C94, $8C9C and $8CA4).
FRONT_WHEEL's second column for the right wheel, eight bytes on along its strip.
The right wheel's third column. From $8CAC its edge, eleven bytes of $1A, $0E and $03, with zeros either side.

Command $41: counts the pixel columns from $60 to $61, kept inside the view ($40-$BF) and widened to whole characters ($41 to $55), once more each at $0240. A column counted for the first time has $C500 set to $C0 and starts at $C1. When $60 is past $61 nothing is counted and bit 7 of $6D and of $C303 is cleared.

Command $42: in each character column from $41 to $55, fills the pixels between the edges at $0240 and those at $C600 with colour 2, by parity: TOGGLE_EDGES flips each pixel's bit in the row flags at $C400 at both its edges, and going up the column a pixel is filled while its bit is set. Bit 7 of a row's flags marks the bottom row of each character row, where going up moves the pointer to the character row above, and $C0 just above the view's top row stops the fill. The flags are flipped back afterwards.
For the four pixel columns from X, each whose edge at $0240 is above its edge at $C600 flips its bit (8, 4, 2 or 1) in the row flags just above the first edge and at the second.
For each set of the four pixels in a byte (bit 3 the leftmost), the mask that turns those pixels from colour 3 to colour 2.

Command $43: the bar above the speedometer's scale (row 21 of the dashboard, from column 12, two pixel rows deep), X/2 pixels long (less 64 from 64 on). Only what changed since the last length ($C34F) is drawn: whole bytes of four pixels and one part byte at the end.
The bar's last byte with one, two and three of its four pixels lit.
A byte of the bar with all four pixels lit.
A byte of the bar with none lit.

Command $44: a value for each of the track's pieces at $0710, from the last piece back to the first. A piece listed at $075E takes its own from $0769, and when that has bit 7 set the three pieces before it get bit 7 too. A piece whose kind (the low four bits at $0400) has bit 7 set at $B240 takes X. Any other takes the value of the piece after it plus 10, up to $7F, carried in $14 (from $7C).
The X PIECE_TABLE was given.
The X CLEAR_VIEW was given: bit 7 draws the bonnet into the bitmap at $4000 too.

Command $45: fills the view in the bitmap being drawn ($12: 0 for $4000) with colour 3, thirteen character rows of 32 characters from $62A0 (or $42A0), and puts back the bonnet below it from its copy at $C000-$C25F; into the bitmap at $4000 only when bit 7 of X is set.

Command $46: for each of the view's 32 character columns whose top character row of colour 2 has moved since the last frame ($0200 was, $0201 now, four bytes a column), sets the colour RAM of the rows between: to $C76B for the rows it rose past, to $0E for those it fell back from. Each character row's address in colour RAM comes from the tables at $A400 (low) and $A418 (high), indexed by pixel row over 8.

Command $47, with the KERNAL in: nothing unless $0840 says there is a drive. X = 0 sends the drive "I0" (initialise); any other X sends "S0:" and the name at $AEC1 (scratch: the old file goes before a save), when $C77B says there is one. Comes back with carry set on an error; "file not found" (4) is not one.
"S0:" and the twelve characters of the file's name, the command DISK_COMMAND sends to scratch a file.
The name, copied from $AEC1.
X = 0: the two bytes of "I0" at $9123 named for SETNAM, then on as for the scratch from $90E3.
"I0", the command that initialises the drive.
The character for each of the 64 keys, by key number (the bit read on port B times 8 plus the bit driven on port A): the first 64 with a shift key held, the next 64 without.
Prints three spaces.
Prints two spaces.
Prints a space.

The tables of a game for several after each round, once every player has raced ($C77F reaching $31A3) and before the next round ($31A2 counted down): BONUS_RESULTS, then RESULTS_TABLE, with $31A5 set meanwhile.
RESULTS_TABLE with $C39C set: the round's race times and bonuses.

The round's bonuses, from row $0E: one more of the table's wins ($C728) to the driver of the fastest race ($C76E) and one more of its fastest laps ($C734) to the driver of the fastest lap ($C76D), each named; then the division sorted again.
A in binary-coded decimal: counts A times from 0 in decimal mode (A = 0 counts 256 times, which gives $56). X is kept, by way of $CE.

Under the results, the records the player has broken ($C305: bit 0 which message, bit 7 the race's record, bit 6 the lap's), each with the holder's name now at $31AA ($D6, $C9) and its time (clocks $0F and $0E).

At the end of the player's lap X: the race's fastest lap so far (clock $0C, its driver into $C76D) and the track's lap record (clock $0E: the player's name into the menus' strings at $C9, $C305 bits 6 and 0); the lap added to the player's race time (clock $31A4 + $0C); and at the race's end (lap 4, $C378) the fastest race (clock $0D, $C76E) and the track's race record (clock $0F: the name at $D6, $C305 bits 7 and 0).
The player's twelve-letter name ($AE01 + 16 $31A4) into the menus' strings at $31AA + Y.

The records of the track raced ($C77D in the order at $3728, the Super League's eight on, $C71A), sixteen bytes in each of the pages under the chips: the lap's at $DE00 and the race's at $DF00, each a twelve-letter holder's name and a time. With A bit 7 set they are put where the race keeps them (the names at $3273 and $3280, the times in clocks $0E and $0F) and the chips banked back in; clear, the race's are kept there, the chips left banked out for the caller.

With A 1 before a save, 0 after a load (nothing otherwise, nor after a failure, for the league of one or for a directory): the Hall of Fame's records, the two pages under the chips at $DE00 and $DF00, copied to $4000 and scrambled; or loaded, unscrambled and merged, each track's record taken from the file when it is faster than the one held. A game for several: LEAGUE_FILE.
A file that fails the check leaves the chips banked out ($01 $34): this RTS skips IO_BACK.
The merge: each record's time (+$0C, three decimal bytes, minutes first) compared, the faster kept.

The name typed ($AEC1) for what it starts with, into $C367: "DIR " a directory ($80; a save becomes a load, $C77B cleared), "HALL" the Hall of Fame ($40), "MP" a game for several (1), anything else the league of one (0). A save of the league with several players, or of a game for several with one, is refused: "File name is not suitable", a key, the message and the name rubbed out, and the carry set.
Refused: the message, a key, and the message and the name rubbed out.
The names FILE_NAME_CHECK looks for: "DIR ", "HALL" and "MP"; the "$" after them is the directory's name for the KERNAL.
"HALL".
"MP", and the directory's name "$".

After a save or a load, unless it was a directory that worked: the file's name and " loaded" or " saved", with " NOT" and why after a failure ($C39A: $80 a problem, $81 incorrect data), and a press of fire. $C39A comes back in A.
Each file message's place in the table at $9535: " loaded", " saved", then by $C39A plus 2 the failures, and by $0840 plus 9 the tape's and the disc's messages before a save.

The file messages, each ended by $FF: " NOT", " loaded", " saved", "Incorrect data found", "File name already exists", "Problem encountered", "File name is not suitable", the message before a save and its "tape" and "disc".
FILE_MESSAGE's loop: each character printed (PRINT_CHAR) and the next taken.
Message X of the table at $9535 (characters to $FF).

The directory loaded at $4000 shown on the KERNAL's screen at $0400: "DIRECTORY:", then the files whose names are twelve characters (a quote at both ends, as the game's own are), three to a row and 54 to a screen, fire for each screen after the first.
An entry is a file of the game's when its line at $4025 + 32n has quotes 13 apart.
Its name copied to the screen, three names to a row.
"DIRECTORY:".
The scrambling's random numbers: the 16-bit seed at $96A6 times 5, and its bits 2 to 9 in A.
The seed, low byte first; SCRAMBLE starts it at $683B.
The scrambling's seed's high byte, $68 as SCRAMBLE starts it.
Scrambles the page at $4000: the 256 numbers of the run from seed $683B at $4300, and a place in them, $F810 (READ_CONTROLS's count, so any), kept in the page's byte $0F; then SCRAMBLE_PAGE.
Unscrambles the page at $4000 the same way, the place taken from its byte $0F.

The page at ($1E), but its byte $0F. Scrambling: bytes $EF, $1F and $FF set to 0 for the check, and each byte replaced by how many numbers of the run, from the place, it took to come to its value; the place then moved on by the number at that count. Unscrambling makes the same draws: each byte the number its count comes to. Then the check: the three bytes 0, or $C39A $81 (incorrect data) and the carry set.
Both pages from $4000 scrambled, the run going on into the second.
Both pages from $4000 unscrambled; the carry is the second page's check.

A game for several in the file at $4000: the players' names ($AE40-$AEBF) at $4020, the league's tables ($C728-$C763) at $40A0, how many players ($31A1) at $40DC and the drivers' places ($83B0) at $40E0, scrambled for a save; unscrambled and put back after a load.

In the pause, with F1 held (key $20), the five keys defined again: a message for each in the order $983C names (messages from $9841), each key taken as it is pressed (a beep, EFFECT 0) and let go; then the five again to confirm, any that differs starting it all over; and the last message.
The keys scanned from $3F down until one is held.
Defining ($983B 1), the key goes into $F807; confirming (0), it must be the one there.
The key being defined, 4 down to 0.
1 while the keys are defined, 0 while they are confirmed.
The place in $F807 of each key in the order asked.
The message (SHOW_MESSAGE's Y) asking for each key.

In a game for several, the five keys READ_CONTROLS reads ($F807) kept for the player whose turn it is ($31A4, the drivers from 4), five bytes each at $987A: put in with A bit 7 set, kept with it clear.
Each player's five keys, as at $F807.

The practice's choices: a division from the menus' strings ($31A0 set), into $31A7 as 3 less the item (skipped once after a practice race, $31A8), then one of its two tracks or Cancel (2), the one before lit ($C76C bit 0). The choice comes back in A.

The Hall of Fame: the records of the league's eight tracks (or the Super League's, $C71A) copied from under the chips to $0400, the bitmap at $4000 cleared and coloured in hi-res, the headings, and for each track (its letters at $99EF) the lap record's holder and time and the race record's; fire, and the league's screen again.
Two letters for each track in the Hall of Fame, the last first.
HALL_OF_FAME reads each pair's second letter from $99F0 + X.
Clock X as minutes, seconds and hundredths (M:SS.HH), or seven dashes when it is 9 minutes or more, or no time at all.
The game's NMI handler, set at $FFFA by the start-up ($4025): it reads CIA 2's interrupt flags ($DD0D) to clear them and returns, so the RESTORE key and CIA 2's timers do nothing.

Where the car (the eye) is on piece $2E: across the road from its middle line into $B7/$B8, along it into $B3/$B4, and the road's direction under it into $0189/$018A. $3D is the turn between the view and the piece (the view's quarter $68 less the piece's direction $1D).
A straight piece: the eye's place in the piece's frame (EYE_IN_PIECE) less the middle line's offset (bytes 2 and 3 of the kind's table at ($9A)); the direction is the piece's own.

A diagonal piece ($B2 bit 6): the frame turned by an eighth, the difference and the sum of the two distances times $B5/256 (one over the square root of two); across less bytes 2 and 3, along times byte 7, and the direction from bytes 4 and 5.

A curve ($B2 bit 7): measured from its centre (bytes 2 to 5, PIECE_POINT_IN_VIEW). PROJECT_X's place across for the centre ($A202/$A29A), with the view's heading ($32/$3E) and quarter, is its bearing; a quarter turn on from it ($9D the curve's side) is the road's direction.
The distance along: the bearing less the piece's start (bytes 6 and 7) and its direction ($1D's quarters), made positive, times byte 8, shifted by a count from $B2's low two bits.
On a piece of kind 1 or 3, a car past its end ($9E points) is moved to the next piece (the one before on a piece driven backwards, $A4) and placed again, unless that piece is of kind 4.
Across: the curve's radius (bytes 9 and 10) less the distance from its centre (CURVE_DISTANCE, then CURVE_DISTANCE_FIX), the other way for a curve to the other side ($9D).

The distance from the curve's centre, a first guess, into $C1/$C2: the logarithm PROJECT_X left in $AB/$AC turned back through the steps at $B000 and $A380, with a straight line to the next step ($B001) by $AB's low three bits, and shifted by its whole part ($AC, in fours).

The road's height at point X of the piece, times 8, in A:$14 (the top three bits that leave A are those of $15): an even point from the left edge's list ($98, added to $3F/$35), an odd one from the right's ($CA, added to $40/$36). Two bytes a point with $A2 bit 7 set, the high seven bits first; otherwise one byte, its low four bits the high byte and its next three the top of the low byte.

The car's place along its piece ($B3/$B4, from the other end on a piece driven backwards) into $22 and $C3; a quarter of a segment on into $8D/$8E ($8E = $80 when that is past the piece's end, $BE), twice the segment after it into $27, and $20 less the segment ($BE more past the end) into $D2 and $D3.

The road's height under each of the car's three points (2, 1, then 0) into $C340/$C343/$C3CE, each from the piece the car is on ($C374). The point's offset from the car's middle ($0130/$0133 across, $0136/$0139 along, over 16) is added to the car's place ($B7/$B8, $B3/$B4).

Across, as a fraction of the road's width ($BC) into $4C, and the player's line $2B from point 2. A point past either edge (from 0 to $0180) is marked in $C3A6 bit 7, with its place in $C3A4/$C3A5, and takes 0 or $FF.
Along, in segments ($BD each): the fraction into $4D and the segment into $BF, twice it into $C0. A point past either end of the piece is on the next one (WHEEL_PIECE_STEP).

The heights of the four corners round the point ($48 and $49 at one end of its segment, $4A and $4B at the other, POINT_HEIGHT), counted from the other end on a piece driven backwards; then the height between them (WHEEL_ROAD_HEIGHT).

The eye's place in the piece's own frame, from the piece's corner as the view sees it ($93:$92 across, $95:$94 along): turned by the quarters between the view and the piece ($3D's top two bits), with a square (8) added where the corner moves, into $77:$51 across and $78:$52 along.

A point past its piece's end is on the next piece ($BF positive; the one before on a piece driven backwards) or the one before: $2E moved and that piece loaded, $C0 its first segment or its last ($9E less 4), and for a piece the other way round the fractions across and along ($4C, $4D) turned round (0 less each, $FF for 0).

The road's height between four corners, $48 and $49 at one end ($5B the top byte) and $4A and $4B at the other ($DC), across by $4C/256 and then along by $4D/256, into $16:$15:$14. A difference too big for sixteen bits is worked an eighth the size and shifted back.

Point X's road height (ROAD_HEIGHT_AT, or OFF_EDGE_HEIGHT for a point past the edge) into $C340/$C343/$C3CE. While the car is slow ($0188 below 10) and nearly level (the pitch's high byte within 4 of none), the average of it and the height there before.

The guess at the distance from the curve's centre ($C1/$C2) made closer: the difference between the square of the true distance ($77:$51 across and $78:$52 along, squared and added) and the guess's square, times the kind's factor ($A01B), over 16, added to it.

The rest of CURVE_DISTANCE_FIX: the difference times the kind's factor (MUL_S16_U8), shifted four places right (SHIFT16), added to the guess at $C1/$C2. $A000 is also the byte SAVE_OR_LOAD keeps on the stack while the KERNAL is banked in and puts back after.
For each kind of piece ($C3CD), the factor CURVE_DISTANCE_FIX corrects a curve's distance by; 0 for kinds 0, 4, 5 and 10.

The point at bytes Y to Y+3 of the kind's table (across and along, in the piece's frame) from the eye: turned by the quarters between the view and the piece ($3D), a square (8) added where the corner moves, plus the corner's place ($93:$92 across, $95:$94 along), into $77:$51 and $78:$52. Y comes back four on.

The height under a point past the road's edge ($C3A4/$C3A5, its place across). Less than $30 past the edge: the road's height ($16:$15:$14) less sixteen times the distance past, and $100 less again when that is below $10000, with $C30A set to $80 or $40 by the side. Further out, or when the height would fall under $1000, $C359 is set (the point is off the edge) and the height is $1000.

The heights of the car's three points from its middle's ($0101/$0104/$0107): less the pitch's sine ($0121/$0124, SINE16) for point 2 ($C348/$C34B/$C3D3), plus it for points 0 and 1 ($C346/$C349/$C3D1 and $C347/$C34A/$C3D2), which are also half the roll's sine ($0123/$0126) above and below that.
The loop of PRINT_STRING_E000.
Prints string X of the table at $E000, up to its $FF; while players are being chosen ($31A0 bit 7), string X of the menus' table at $31AA instead.
Prints string X of the menus' table at $31AA, up to its $FF.
Fourteen bytes of code that nothing calls: Y times 24, plus 8, back in Y.
$E8, which REQUEST_FLIP and TRACK_PREVIEW add $18 to: $00, the value of $12 that draws into the bitmap at $4000. Then eleven letters that nothing reads, "FKSRFUHBERD".
DRAW_PIECE reads $A1FE + X, X the piece's number of points: the low byte of its next-to-last point's place across, from the table at $A200, which it copies to point 30 at $A21E.
DRAW_PIECE reads $A1FF + X: the low byte of the piece's last point's place across, which it copies to point 31 at $A21F.
128 high bytes of $800 times 2 to the power n/128, for n from 0 to 127 ($0800 up to $0FD4); the low bytes are at $B000. CURVE_DISTANCE turns a logarithm back into a distance with them.

For SET_ROW_COLOURS, by pixel row over 8: the low byte of the colour RAM's address for that character row, from column 4 ($D804 for 6, the view's top, and 40 on for each row after; $D800 for 0 to 5). LINE_COLOUR's mask table for colour 0 is also $A400, read from $A440 on.
The high bytes of the same 24 addresses, $D8 to $DA.
Sixteen bytes that nothing reads: pieces of code (STA $33, LDA $31, STA $32, LDA #0, STA $31, BEQ, LSR $31, ROR $32).

The masks that clear a multicolour pixel to colour 0, $3F, $CF, $F3 and $FC, repeated for each pixel column from $40 to $BF: the line drawer ANDs the bitmap with $A400 + X (LINE_COLOUR's table for X 0).
The masks that leave a multicolour pixel colour 1, $7F, $DF, $F7 and $FD, for pixel columns $40 to $BF from $A480 + X (LINE_COLOUR's table for X 1); DUST_PLOT reads them as $A4C0 + its column.
The last 64 of those masks. $A500 is also the base of the bitmap's row tables: BITMAP_BYTE, DUST_BYTE, the line drawer and the fills add $A500 + Y for pixel row Y from $40 on.

For each pixel row from $40 to $FF (the view from its top), the low byte of its bitmap address at column 4, less the row's number, so that ($1E),Y reaches it: $4260 for row $40, the view's top at $42A0.

07 06 05 04 03 02 01 00, twice. BITMAP_BYTE, DUST_BYTE, the line drawer and the fills read $A600 plus the row as the high byte of the row's address, but their rows start at $40, so these sixteen, rows 0 to 15, are never read; what they were for is unknown.

For PROJECT_LOG and PROJECT_Y, added to a logarithm's high byte for the number of places Y it was shifted to fit eight bits: $E0 plus four times the shifts, for 0 to 7, then the same again for the eight Ys of a negative number.
The opponent car's width on the screen by its distance, 32 bytes from $1B down to $07 (OPP_CORNERS).
The high bytes of the row tables, for pixel rows $40 to $FF, less the row's number with the low byte's carry.
The quarter-wave table, 256 bytes from $FF down to $01: the cosine of a quarter turn in 256 steps, which read from its far end is the sine (SIN_COS, SINE16, ROLL_TABLES, WHEEL_SPRITES, PROJECT_LOG).
SINE16 reads the next step from $A701 for its straight line between two.
EXP's results for the lowest band of logarithms, $E000 to $EFFF: 128 bytes from 1 up, read by the logarithm's top bits.
EXP's results for $F000 to $F7FF, 128 bytes.
EXP's results for $F800 to $FFFF, 256 bytes, up to $FF.
The low bytes of 1,024 times the base-2 logarithm of n, for n from 0 to 255 (PROJECT_LOG, PROJECT_Y); n = 0 gives $F100, a large negative number.
The high bytes of the logarithms: $00 for 1, $04 for 2, $08 for 4, $1F near 255.
EXP's rounding for its lowest band: the result is one more when the logarithm's fraction is at least this byte; $FF never.
EXP's rounding for the middle band, the same way.

Two tables packed into one. The top five bits are EXP's rounding thresholds for its highest band (EXP ANDs with $F8); the low three bits are extra bits of precision for the quarter-wave table, which SINE16 reads from $AD00 and $AD01.
SINE16 reads the next step's three extra bits from $AD01.

Loaded: the pool of twelve opponents, sixteen bytes each, which the start-up copies to $DC00: a space, the name, spaces, and two more bytes. Hot Rod, Whizz Kid, Bad Guy, The Dodger, Big Ed, Max Boost, Dare Devil, High Flyer, Bully Boy, Jumping Jack, Road Hog, and a twelfth of spaces. START puts the whole pool back here from $DC00, and NEW_DRIVERS copies a league's opponents from it.
The names' letters, $AE01 + 16 times the driver: RECORD_NAME reads the player's from here, and the menus write a name typed here.
In a game for several, the players' names, $AE40-$AEBF, which LEAGUE_FILE saves and loads. Loaded: Big Ed's slot and the ones after.
The twelve letters in the last slot, which SAVE_CODE puts into the league's save code (EOR $3B). Loaded: spaces.
The name typed for a file (NAME_ENTRY_AT), which FILE_NAME_CHECK checks and DISK_COMMAND sends. Loaded: pieces of code that nothing runs.
Each of the twelve drivers' flags, how it drives (OPPONENT_LINE, OPP_WHEELS): copied to $DCE0 with the pool, and back here by NEW_DRIVERS. After the twelve, pieces of code that nothing runs.
The eight tracks' names, sixteen bytes each, padded with spaces: LITTLE RAMP, STEPPING STONES, HUMP BACK, BIG RAMP, SKI JUMP, DRAW BRIDGE, HIGH JUMP, ROLLER COASTER.

The sound effects, eight bytes each for START_EFFECT (EFFECT A reads $AF80 + 8A): the slot, the control byte, attack and decay, sustain and release, the pitch's high byte, the pulse's, and the frames the gate is held; the eighth, $80, is not read. Effect 0 is the keys' beep, a short pulse note.

Effect 1's pitch, the noise of the stones under the car: DUST_GO and DAMAGE write it before they start the effect. Then effects 2 to 6, and at $AFB8 eight bytes no call asks for, which do not read as an effect.
The matrix entries VELOCITY_TO_CAR multiplies the velocity's three axes by, three to a list (their places, X for MUL_S16_MATRIX): this one for the speed along the road.
The second list for VELOCITY_TO_CAR.
The third list for VELOCITY_TO_CAR.
The entries FORCES_TO_WORLD turns the forces' first world axis with.
FORCES_TO_WORLD's second list.
FORCES_TO_WORLD's third list.
The two entries SPIN_TO_ANGLES turns the spin into the pitch's speed with.
The two for the roll's speed. After them, from $AFE0, nothing reads "COPYRIGHT GEOFF CRAMMOND 1988", hidden by an EOR with $AA on every byte.
The low bytes of $800 times 2 to the power n/128 (the high bytes at $A380): CURVE_DISTANCE takes step n from here.
CURVE_DISTANCE's next step, for the straight line between two by the logarithm's low three bits.
For COSINE_OF, 128 bytes: the cosine of an angle whose sine is twice the index over 256, as a byte, $FF down to $20.

The pieces' kinds' tables, a pointer for each of the sixteen kinds (PIECE_LOAD by the low four bits of $0400). Kinds 0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 10 point at tables from $B250; the other nine hold bytes that do not point at tables.
PIECE_LOAD reads each pointer's high byte from $B101.
128 pointers to the shapes, which BUILD_TRACK gives each piece two of ($049C and $04EA) and PIECE_LOAD and DRAWBRIDGE read. Four of them ($20A7, $20A3, $A37D and $20AA) point outside the shapes.
The shape pointers' high bytes.
The eight tracks' descriptions, for BUILD_TRACK by track number: $BA62 to $BE82. Then sixteen bytes that are not pointers.
BUILD_TRACK reads each track pointer's high byte from $B221.
A byte for each of the sixteen kinds: bit 7 for kinds a race cannot start on (START_PLACE) and that PIECE_TABLE gives X, read by OPPONENT_LINE too.

Kind 0's table. Byte 0 says where its counts start and byte 1 is its flags ($B2: bit 7 a curve, bit 6 a diagonal); bytes 2 to 10 its geometry for PLACE_ON_PIECE (the line's offset, or a curve's centre, direction and radius); then the number of points and the bytes PIECE_LOAD keeps, and from seven bytes on the road's points, four to a segment (OPP_SEGMENT_POINTS).
Kind 1's table, laid out as kind 0's.
Kind 3's table.
Kind 4's table.
Kind 6's table.
Kind 7's table.
Kind 10's table, the last, to $B50C.
The shapes, the first of 128, to $BA61: the points of a piece's road, which PIECE_LOAD takes through $98/$99 and $CA/$CB.
Shape 64 on.

Little Ramp, 44 pieces. A track's description for BUILD_TRACK: its piece count and three more bytes, where it starts, then each piece's kind and flags, square and shapes ($F repeats the last piece), and after the pieces the start line's piece, the length, six bytes for $C774 and the lists for $075E/$0769 and $0190.
Stepping Stones, 56 pieces.
Hump Back, 53 pieces.
Big Ramp, 44 pieces.
Ski Jump, 40 pieces.
Draw Bridge, 78 pieces.
High Jump, 52 pieces.
Roller Coaster, 78 pieces, the last track, to $BF41.
Zeros after the last track, to $BFA9.
For OPP_PICK, by track in the league: a random number ANDed with this byte ...
... and added to this one is the opponent's top speed for the race ($2099).
The same for the second limit ($209A): the mask ...
... and the base.
The Super League's four tables, read at track plus $20 while $C71A is set: the top speed's mask,
its base,
the second limit's mask,
and its base.
Eleven bytes CLEAR_RACE copies to $C382-$C38C at the start of each race, from $BFEA plus $C71A, so one byte further on in the Super League.
Ten bytes after them that nothing reads.
Scratch for MUL_S8_U8's negated product.
Scratch for MUL_S16_MATRIX: the matrix entry's high byte, its sign.
The sign byte SHIFT16 shifts in from the top: $00 or $FF.
Where SIN_COS keeps X while it works.
Multiplies A by $15, both unsigned, by shift and add: the product's high byte comes back in A and its low byte in $14. The carry always comes back clear. Every multiply in the game goes through here.
Tests one key: X is its number in the keyboard matrix (row times 8 plus column). Asks the command dispatcher (command $81) to scan that key and gives back Z set when it is held. Y is kept.

The sine and cosine of the angle in A (high) and $14 (low), a whole turn being $10000. Rounds the angle to the table's 512 steps (adds $0020), then reads the quarter-wave table at $A700 twice, once forward and once mirrored, to give the two signed results in $56 and $57. $58 keeps the rounded angle's high byte and $59 two bits that tell the callers which quadrant it is in, so they can set the signs. X is kept.
Multiplies the signed byte in A by the magnitude in $15, whose sign is bit 7 of $5A: the signed 16-bit product comes back in A (high) and $14 (low).
Clears the sign in $5A and runs on into MUL_S16_S8: the signed 16-bit number in A:$14 times the positive factor in $15, divided by 256.

Multiplies the signed 16-bit number in A (high) and $14 by the factor in $15, whose sign is bit 7 of $5A, and keeps the top two bytes of the product: A:$14 times $15 over 256, signed. $5A comes back holding the product's sign.

Multiplies the signed 16-bit number in A:$14 by entry X of the car's rotation matrix (the two bytes at $0774,X and $079C,X, of which it uses a quarter, eight bits, as the factor) and divides by 256. The result in A:$14 is signed. This is how the physics turns a vector from one frame of reference to the other, one term at a time.
The tail the signed multiplies share: $16 and $14 hold the magnitude, $15 the factor and A the sign byte; works out both partial products, adds them and applies the sign.
Negates the two-byte number in A (high) and $14 when the N flag is set on entry, so a caller can test a sign (a BIT or a load) and call this straight after. With N clear it returns at once.
Negates the two-byte number in A (high) and $14, two's complement. $15 is left holding the high byte it was given.

The sine of the angle in A (high) and $14 (low), a whole turn being $10000, as a signed number in A:$14: the quarter-wave table at $A700, read from its far end for an angle in the first or third quarter (bit 6 clear), with a straight line between two neighbouring steps by the angle's low bits and the extra precision at $AD00; bit 7 of the angle gives the sign. An angle less than $40 from 0 or from a half turn gives 0 at once.
Entry X of the rotation matrix ($0774,X and $079C,X) times 5/16, as a half plus an eighth, halved, and negated when $5A is negative. Comes back in A:$14.
Squares the signed 16-bit number in A (high) and Y (low) into the four bytes $16-$19, by three 8-bit multiplies.

Shifts the signed number in A (high) and $14 by Y bits: right for Y from 1 to $7F, the sign coming in from the top, and left for Y from $80 up (by 256 minus Y), the bits that leave the top collecting in $2D. Y = 0 leaves it alone. The sign it shifts in runs out after eight places, so a negative number shifted further right picks up zeros.

The car's rotation matrix from its three angles, once a step of the world: the sines and cosines (SIN_COS) of the heading ($0122/$0125), of the heading less the drift ($0189/$018A) and of the pitch ($0121/$0124); the products of pairs into entries $06, $08, $1A and $1C (MATRIX_PRODUCT) and $02, $03, $22 and $23 (MATRIX_PRODUCT_TC), and single terms into $04, $1E, $20, $0A, $0C and $0E (MATRIX_TERM), with $07AC set to 4 and $0784 to 0. Each entry from $06 to $10 and from $1A to $20 is then corrected through the tables at $0300/$0380 and $C310-$C334, indexed by its own size and sign, and made two's complement as its sign and $0126 say; seven more are sums and differences of others ($0786-$078C, high bytes $07AE-$07B4).
Each entry corrected: the next one up ($0775/$079D) from $0300 and $C328/$C334, its own from $0380 and $C310/$C31C, halved.
The entries made from others.
Y times $15 (MUL8), times 4 and rounded, into matrix entry X: low byte at $0774 + X, high at $079C + X with bit 7 the sign the caller's N flag gave, sign and size.
A times 4 into entry X, with Y's bit 7 as the sign in bit 7 of the high byte.
MATRIX_PRODUCT, then MATRIX_TO_TC.
Entry X from sign and size to two's complement.

The car's velocity ($0109-$010B, high bytes $010F-$0111) turned into the car's frame for two of its axes, each the sum of three products with the matrix entries listed at $AFC0, $AFC3 and $AFC6 (MUL_S16_MATRIX): the speeds along the road at $0154/$0157 and $0156/$0159.

A fixed pull along one of the world's axes seen in the car's frame: matrix entries $0F, $04 and $0E times 5/16 (FIVE_SIXTEENTHS with $5A set, the last negated back) into $0140/$013D, $0141/$013E and $013F/$013C.

The forces in the car's frame ($015A-$015C, high bytes $015D-$015F) turned into the world's, each axis the sum of three products with the entries listed at $AFC9, $AFCC and $AFCF: the forces at $0115-$0117 and $011B-$011D.

The car's spin ($010C/$010D, high bytes $0112/$0113) turned into the speeds of its pitch and roll ($016A/$016D and $016B/$016E) by the entries listed at $AFD2 and $AFD4; the heading's speed ($016C/$016F) is the spin's third axis ($010E/$0114) plus the roll's speed times entry 4.

The menus' bands: with $3DF8 bit 0 set, multicolour from the top to line $72 and hi-res below; otherwise multicolour with a black background from line $CE, the background dark grey ($0B) from line $D5, and hi-res from line $28.

The raster interrupt. Anything else that interrupts (a CIA) is acknowledged and left. With $3DF8 clear it does nothing more; with it positive it splits the menus' screen into bands ($CD5C); otherwise the race's: above line $80 the view's top band, from it the bands below. Each band sets the line of the next and returns through $CF49.
The race's top band: the bitmap shown ($D018 $70 or $78) by $C35F, which takes $C370 unless a flip is waiting ($C37A).
While a message is up ($C355), its two sprites at the top of the view (pointers $FE and $FF, colour $C399) until line $64.

Sprites 2 and 3 placed for the dashboard's clocks, and while the boost's flame shows ($72 bit 7) sprites 0 and 1 for it, the two frames of its table in turn ($C36D); the sprites $6E names on; the next band at line $C5.
The bands below: from line $C5 the bitmap at $78 shown and the flip seen ($C37B from $C37A), the next at line $D7.
From line $D7, the dashboard: sprites 0 to 3 at the bottom (places across at $140D-$1410), black and hi-res, $6F's sprites on.

The engine's note ($09/$0A) moved on by $10/$11 (0 if it goes below), into voice 1 and, an octave down, voice 3; the sound effects' frame (EFFECT_TICK); and the engine's count $5F moved on by $5D, the front wheels turning at each carry (WHEELS_TURN). The next band at line $3D.
The next band's line into $D012, its ninth bit cleared.
The boost's flame, sprites 0 and 1, for the two frames the interrupt alternates ($C36D): sprite 0's place across, low byte.
Sprite 1's place across, low byte.
Sprite 0's place down.
Sprite 1's place down.
Sprite 0's pointer for each frame, four on for the bitmap at $70 ($C35F bit 7).
Sprite 1's pointer, the same.
The high bits of the sprites' places across ($D010) for each frame.
Sound effect A, from its seven bytes at $AF80 plus eight times A (START_EFFECT).

Before a line across the road: each of the pair's two points (point $C6 and its neighbour) more than $50 from the middle of the screen across ($A200/$A298 less $80) has a quarter of the excess added to its height on the screen ($A24C/$A2E4).
Adds the two-byte number in $19:$18 to A (high) and $14, leaving the sum in A:$14 and the carry. $15 is left holding the A it was given.
Moves $2E, the piece being drawn, on to the next round the track ($C764 pieces), into X too.
Moves $2E back to the piece before.
Waits for left ($C34C up, carry set), right ($C34C down, carry set) or fire (carry clear), reading the joystick ($F79E).
WHEEL_SPRITES writes the wheels' sprites' heights at $CFFF + Y, the video chip's registers from $D000; the byte here, $6B, nothing reads.

The menus' strings for PRINT_STRING_E000, each ended by $FF, three of them starting with $1F and two bytes that move the print to a column and row: SELECT, Practise, Start the Racing Season, Load/Save/Replay, Load, Save, Replay, Cancel, LOAD from Tape, LOAD from Disc, SAVE to Tape, SAVE to Disc, Filename?, to the SUPER LEAGUE, SUPER DIVISION, EXCELLENT DRIVING - WELL DONE, Hall of Fame.
The row of the SUPER DIVISION heading, which DIVISION_AT writes.
Stops the three sound effects (command $15 for slots 2, 1 and 0).

The engine's note, once a race pass. The aim is the speed along the road ($0156/$0159, its size) while $6A is set; otherwise 0, or $C8 while either of $66's low bits is set; plus 5. An eighth of the gap from the note $09/$0A to the aim is the step $10/$11 the interrupt adds, held to $0100 going up and to $FF00 going down ($FFE0 while $6A is clear, unless the step is already smaller). Then the pulse widths of voices 1 and 3 from RANDOM, and the filter's cut-off from the aim, between $6E and $E6.

Called as the track's drawing reaches the opponent's piece: draws the opponent there (DRAW_OPPONENT) unless $C36A bit 7 is set or the cars are less than 10 apart ($39/$3A). With $6B bit 7 set and $2F clear it is only marked in $C366, to be drawn later.

Draws the opponent's car: its corners at $C505-$C50A projected into points $3C-$3F (PROJECT_CORNER); $C3DA set when either pair's first point is above its second on the screen; then its frame from points $3C and $3E (CAR_FRAME) and, unless that is off the screen, its sides, end and roof as lines (CAR_SIDES, CAR_ROOF). When $C3DA is set, or $C9 is clear, or the car's place $37/$38 is behind any of $07CC-$07CE (which also sets $6D), the car goes into the fill's tables first (FC31, $C303) and its columns are marked (CMD_MARK_COLUMNS). The line drawer's colour from $C3AB is put back after.
For each of $E8-$EB: a half, a quarter and an eighth of its size, with its sign, into $EC, $F0 and $F4 onwards.
The car's two sides and its end, in the order that keeps the nearer side last ($EA's sign): CAR_SIDE_B, CAR_END, CAR_SIDE_A or the reverse.
The car's end, four corners at points $44-$47 from the frame's centre and its halves, quarters and eighths ($E9-$F6), placed on the screen (PLACE_POINTS), copied to $40-$43 and drawn (CAR_PANEL).
Four points from X: each offset at $A240 and $A28C (doubled when $FC says the frame was halved) added to the frame's centre $F8/$F9 and $FA/$FB, and held to the screen's 0 to 255.
The car's side drawn when the frame's centre is right of the view's left edge ($F8 $40 or more): its corners from the negative of $E8 and $EA (CAR_PANEL_AT).
The car's other side, when the frame's centre is left of the view's right edge ($F8 below $C0): its corners from $E8 less $EC and $EA less $EE.
A side panel's four corners at points $40-$43, from the corner in $D9/$DA (X) and A (Y), the frame's halves $EC/$EE and the offsets $E9/$EB, placed on the screen (PLACE_POINTS) and drawn (CAR_PANEL).
Draws the panel at points $40-$43: edges 40-43 and 41-42 as the fill's edges (FEAB), and lines 43-42 and 40-41 in the order $EA's sign gives.

The frame of the car from points X and X+2 on the screen: its centre into $F8/$F9 (across) and $FA/$FB (down), half the gap between them each way into $51/$77 and $52/$78, its size into $E8-$EB (the across and down halves, held to $5A, and halved again with $FC set to $FF when either is $40 or more), then CAR_FRACTIONS. Carry set when the centre is off the screen (a high byte not 0).

The opponent's car on the track, each pass: its piece and segment (OPP_SEGMENT from 64 back), the pieces' heights there ($9C14 into $48-$4B, $DD/$DE), the segment's four points into $C500-$C503 (OPP_SEGMENT_POINTS) and the car's place along it ($9C, E628), its width from the cars' gap ($A620 by the distance), the left and right of its line $B0 by that width (FF94, E631), and the car's front and back corners at $C505-$C50A (OPP_BODY). Leaves the piece the car's back is on (OPP_SEGMENT from $FF, or 0 when wrecked).

The piece and segment A behind the opponent's place ($23/$C4): the piece into $2E and $A6, from $C375 or the one before it (PIECE_BEHIND, F02F) when the place is in the piece behind; the segment into $A3 ($BE less 1 there) and $18.
The heights of the next piece's points X and X+1 ($9C14) into $DD and $DE, with $DF from the first's high bits.
Point Y set to point X moved towards point X+2 by $17 parts in 128 of the gap (at $C500/$C510, or $C520/$C530 when called with $20 added); with $C30B bit 7 set, from point X+2 towards X+4.
Point Y is point X plus $14/$15.
The opponent's place along its segment ($9C) plus the wheel's offset at $C30D (X), as a fraction into point Y (OPP_ALONG_AT); $C30B bit 7 says it ran into the next segment.
Point Y set A parts in 128 of the way from point X to X+2, across and along (POINT_ALONG twice).
Point Y of $C500-$C530 projected into the view as point X (PROJECT_X, PROJECT_Y, ROLL_POINT).

The opponent's front and back corners: the direction from point $C505 to $C507 (across, then along) times 1.5 into $56/$43 and $57/$44, and corners $C508 and $C50A set out from $C505 and $C507 by it at right angles. The place along ($9C) moved on by half a segment ($4D), into the next segment's heights when it runs over ($48-$4B from $4A, $4B, $DD, $DE), and FF94 with X = 2 on the line $B0.
Three bytes OPP_BODY loads into Y and never reads.

The car's roof: four corners at points $48-$4B from the frame's halves ($EC-$EF), placed (PLACE_POINTS); then the pillars from the end's corners ($44-$47) to the roof's, the roof's edges and the two sides, in the order that hides the far ones: by where the end sits against the roof across ($A245/$A246 against $A249/$A24A), down ($A291/$A292 against $A295/$A296), and whether the car is seen from below ($C3DA), which also draws into the fill's tables first (FCB3).
Lines 44-48 and 45-49.
Lines 47-4B and 46-4A.
Line 49-4A.
Line 44-48.
Line 47-4B.
Line 48-4B.
Line 45-49.
Line 46-4A.
The four points of segment A of the piece at ($9A) into $C500-$C503 (PIECE_POINT, from the piece's point table seven bytes in), counted from the far end when the piece is driven backwards ($A4).
Point Y of the piece (PIECE_POINT) into slot X of $C500-$C530.

A new league: the race's state cleared (CLEAR_RACE), the league's 128 bytes at $C700 cleared while RANDOM is drawn 128 times, the order 0-11 into $C70C, the season reset (RESET_SEASON), and $C719 set to 10.

The races the player does not drive: each driver's rating for this race, its base at $E8B6 plus 0-63 at random, into $C71C; then in each division (only the players' one with several players) the race's two drivers (RACE_PAIR), its result (RACE_RESULT) and the division's table sorted (SORT_DIVISION).
Each driver's base rating, by place in the league's order: 120 for the first, down by ten to 10 for the twelfth.

The places of division $C360 in the league's order, from $50 up to $8A: three places from $E8E1 (9, 6, 3 or 0 for $C360 0 to 3, divisions 4 to 1), or with several players all from 11 less their number up to 12.
The first place of each division in the league's order: 9, 6, 3, 0.

The two drivers of race $C77F of the division into $C771 and $C772, and the player's driver into $31A4: with one player, two of the division's three from the pairs at $E920/$E926, the player always 11; with several, driver 11 less $C77F against the player whose turn it is ($31A2).
Each of the six races' first driver, a place in the division: 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1.
Each race's second driver: 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2. Each pair meets twice.

A race worked out: both drivers' races counted at $C740. $51 bit 7 says the first driver ($C771) won, bit 6 that it set the best lap. A race with the player's driver takes both from the player's own race ($C362, flipped when the player is the first). Otherwise the higher rating ($C71C) wins, a tie at random; bit 6 starts set 96 times in 256 and flips with the winner, so the winner takes the best lap 160 times in 256. The win counts at $C728, the best lap at $C734, and in the player's division both are kept at $C76F and $C770.

The division's points into $C74C, two for each win and one for each best lap, and its table at $C758 sorted by them, a bubble sort: wins break a tie, then with several players the lower driver number, otherwise a coin (RANDOM).
The next byte of the track's description, at ($1E) plus Y.
A track piece's square ($30) one step on by $15's top bits: $10 added with neither set, 1 added with bit 6, $10 taken with bit 7, 1 taken with both.

Track X built from its description (from the pointers at $B220): its piece count and three more bytes into $C764-$C767, where it starts ($51/$77, $52/$78); then for each piece its kind and flags ($0400), its square on the map ($044E), its two shapes ($049C and $04EA, fixed ones from $EBDB/$EBDD for kinds $C-$F), the distance round the track to it ($0670/$06BE, in 32nds), its ends across and along ($0538/$0586, $05D4/$0622) from the shapes' offsets. A kind of $F repeats the last piece the number of times in its top four bits, a square on in the piece's direction each time. Then the piece after the start line ($C77C), the track's length ($C768/$C769), six bytes at $C774, the pairs at $075E/$0769 ($C778 of them) and the bytes at $0190 ($C779), the opponent picked (OPP_PICK) and its table built (command $44).

The two shapes of the fixed pieces, kinds $C-$F, are read from $EBE7 and $EBE9 on: $EBE7-$EBEA holds 3, 4, 4, 3; kind $E's second shape would be the first byte of SHAPE_OFFSET_B's code, and kind $F never gets here.

BUILD_TRACK reads the fixed pieces' second shapes from $EBDD plus the kind, so from $EBE9 for kinds $C-$F. The code here ends BUILD_TRACK: the opponent picked (OPP_PICK) and its table built (command $44, X from $209A).
The first shape of kinds $C and $D, and the second of $C and $D (3, 4, 4, 3, from $EBDB and $EBDD plus the kind).
SHAPE_OFFSET from the piece's second shape (its pointer $CA copied into $98).
The offset of the shape at ($98) at point Y, in A with its fraction in $14 (eighths): two bytes a point when $A2 bit 7 is set, otherwise one byte holding both.

The start of a race, while the count $2F runs down. From $E6 up: the chains' top $C3DF set ($2C, or $D4 with $C36F bit 7) and $34 cleared. At $E5: the chains swung in (CRANE_SWING with 0) and the car lowered (CRANE_LOWER 3). At $E4: lowered (4) and the chains swung out ($FF); once they are there, the count set to $A0-$BF at random ($8C in practice) and message 4 shown (from $2C, or $3C with $C37C bit 7). Below $E4: swung in, lowered (2) and the count taken on, not past 1; the car is let go ($2F, $6B and $C355 cleared, $C37C set to $80) once the count is below $80, or with $C37C set once $C398 is clear.
The car's height ($0171/$0174) brought down by an eighth of its height over the road ($46/$64 less $C35D/$C35E, less A), by at most $0200 a pass. Returns A plus 2.

The chains' top ($C3DF, with $34 below it) moved by A (the other way with $C36F bit 7) until it is at $10 (or $F0); the car's point at $0123/$0126 set under it, less the car's place across ($B5/$B6 over 32); $014E/$014F cleared. Z set when the chains are there.

The car's position moved on the ground: matrix entries $02 and $03 ($0776/$079E, negated, and $0777/$079F), each times $A0/256 with $C36F's sign (MUL_S16_S8) and then times 8 (SHIFT16 with Y $FD), so five times the entry, added to axes 2 and 0 of the position ($0100/$0103/$0106 plus X, three bytes an axis).

A driver's name typed in the panel, for the player being added ($31A1): the panel cleared and framed, "NAME?", the prompt > at column $0E of row $10, and the name into driver 11 - $31A1's place at $AE00 (NAME_ENTRY_AT, with the line under it from X $64, Y $BD).

Up to twelve characters typed into $AE01 + A, the start of a sixteen-byte name, under a line drawn where they go (HLINE at X, Y, $0B long). Return ends it, the rest of the twelve filled with spaces. Letters, figures and . / : take their place (with A's bits 7 and 6 both set, as for a file's name, a small letter as its capital), a space only after the first character, and DEL rubs one out; nothing else counts. The C= key (code 1) cancels a file's name (A $C0), setting $EE35 bit 7, which is otherwise cleared.
A pause, then a key (WAIT_KEY), its character in A.
A character taken: a small letter as its capital for a file's name, and none past the twelfth.
Return: the rest of the name filled with spaces.
Bit 7 set when a file's name was cancelled with the C= key.

A numbered list in the panel, items 0 to Y, each item's string $F001 + X + its number of the table at $E000, A the item lit at the start. The list is drawn again at each change; the item lit is in colour 7, and in colour $0A once fire picks it. The controls let go first; then fire takes the item lit, a number key ($F80C) the item of its number, and forward or back move the light up or down. After the divisions' list (string $18) each item's number; after a division's tracks (string $1C) each track's name. The item chosen comes back in A.
The list drawn, from the top ($19).
The item lit: colour 7, or $0A once chosen ($0F).
After the divisions' strings, the item's number; after the tracks', the track's name ($3728 by $31A7).
Chosen: the text back on the rows, a pause, and the item in A.
The controls let go, a pause, then a change looked for.
Fire chooses ($0F). Otherwise the number keys, from the list's last down.
Forward lights the item above, back the one below.
The Hall of Fame (0) or Practise (1).
Practise: a division and a track, then a return with the track picked ($C76C, $31A8 set).
The Racing Season: the save code made ($F6D7) and $C76C bit 7 set.

The main menu, and after a practice race straight back to the choice of track ($31A8). Its items: 0 the Hall of Fame (HALL_OF_FAME); 1 Practise (a division and a track, PRACTICE_TRACK, and a return with the track picked); 2 the Racing Season (lit once one has begun, $C76C bit 7: the save code made and $C76C set); 3 a second list of Load, Save, Replay and Cancel.
Load, Save, Replay or Cancel.

Replay: the season's points cleared; with F1 held (key $20) the game starts again at START, the players chosen afresh. Otherwise, for one player, the season again from the random numbers its save code kept (SAVE_CODE); when that code does not read back, or with several players, a new league.

Load (0) or Save (1), into $C77B: the league's 256 bytes at $8000 kept at $7B00 and $C77E at $F000, tape or disc asked for (into $0840), the save code made, and SAVE_OR_LOAD. A name cancelled goes straight back to the menu.

The league kept is put back after a save, after a failure, and after a load whose save code does not read back ($C39A $81, incorrect data), but not for the Hall of Fame, a directory or a game for several ($C367).
The result (FILE_RESULT), then the league's screen again.
$C77E kept here while a file is saved or loaded.

Each menu item's string in the table at $E000 (or $31AA while players are chosen), by MENU_CHOICE's X plus the item: the main menu from 0, Load/Save/Replay/Cancel from 4, the loads' Tape/Disc/Cancel from 8 and the saves' from $0C, the players' choices from $10 and $14, the divisions from $18 and a division's tracks from $1C.
Y times 24, plus 8 (with the carry from the doubling), in A and Y: where part Y's two cells start in the damage bar along the dashboard's top, for BAR_HOLE and BAR_HOLE_LIT.

Piece X's shapes and place: its first shape's points ($049C into $A2, their table $98/$99 from $B120) and its second's ($04EA, the table $CA/$CB, its top bit doubled into $D8); its ends ($0538/$0586 into $3F/$35, $05D4/$0622 into $40/$36); its direction ($1D, the top two bits of $0400), whether it is driven backwards ($A4, bit 4 moved to bit 7) and its kind ($C3CD, the low four bits). From the kind's table ($9A/$9B, from $B100): the flags $B2, the number of points $9E (with $62 two less and $BE half less one), $9D (bit 0 of the next byte, as bit 7), $BC, $BD and $C8.

Piece X's square on the map ($044E: across in the low four bits, along in the high) less the view's ($5C, $5E), turned to the view's quarter ($68's top two bits), times 8 plus $CF and $D1, into $93 and $95.
The square next to square X on the map, across or along by which of A and Y is the larger and whether their sum carries, and the piece on it (PIECE_FROM_HERE); A comes back $FF at the map's edge.

The car's place in squares and within its square: axes 0 and 2 of its position, $0100/$0103/$0106 (a low byte of 0 made 1 first), doubled into $AF/$B1 and $5C/$5E, and the place within the square into $45/$63/$24 and $47/$65/$26, copied or taken from a whole square (VIEW_COPY, VIEW_NEGATE) and swapped as A's top two bits, the view's quarter, say.
Axis X of the car's position, three bytes ($0100, $0103, $0106 plus X), taken from 8 squares into $45, $63 and $24 plus Y.
Axis X of the car's position, three bytes ($0100, $0103, $0106 plus X), into $45, $63 and $24 plus Y.

The view put where the car is. Its quarter ($68) from the car's heading ($0125, rounded by $20), its square and its place in it (VIEW_SQUARE), and its height over 8 ($0101/$0104/$0107 into $46/$64). The eye's height $37/$38: the height plus $0160/$0161 (doubled when $0161 is 5 or more, then with $80 and 7, or 2, added) less the car's tilt when it leans one way ($0121/$0124 halved), over 16. The place across and along within the square over 16 and negated ($CF/$92, $D1/$94), and the heading less $20 times 4 at $32, its negative at $A7/$A8 ($3E is set to $FF).

The car's place across the road: $B7/$B8 less $C0 (the other way on a piece driven backwards, $A4) into $B5/$B6. Once that is a whole unit or more either way the car is off the road: $6B set to $80, $C36F to its side, $C368 to 15 and the dust cleared (DUST_CLEAR), unless $6B bit 7 was set already. On the road $6B and $C373 are cleared, unless $6B bit 6 is set.
The track from above: for each of the 17 rows of squares from the eye ($00-$10), the squares from 0 to the left as far as -8, then from 1 to the right as far as 8 (MAP_SQUARE; $C361 says which side).

The square X across and Y along from the eye, turned to the view's quarter ($68) into $0B/$0C, and the piece on it ($FF6A) drawn whole (DRAW_PIECE, POINTS_TO_LINES) when there is one. X and Y come back as they were.

The track seen from above before a race, from the side $C34C chooses: the eye's place and heading from $F3FC, $F400 and $F404, its height $03F0 ($0104/$0107), the horizon $12 at $18 more than $A1F2 and $33 at $B8; the view started (NEW_VIEW), the columns' limits at $C640 set to $C0, three bands of the bitmap ($52E0, $5420 and $5560, 256 bytes each) filled with $FF, and the screen on (SCREEN_ON). Every square is then drawn (MAP_SQUARES) with $262B set to $0B and PROJECT_X's first three bytes rewritten to the JMP at $F408, both put back after.
The eye's place across ($0106) for each of TRACK_PREVIEW's four sides.
The eye's place along ($0108) for each side.
The eye's heading ($0125) for each side: a quarter turn apart.
The JMP to PROJECT_X_PAIR that TRACK_PREVIEW writes over PROJECT_X's first three bytes.

What PROJECT_X runs while TRACK_PREVIEW has rewritten its first bytes to a JMP here: the depth ($77:$51) halved, then the distance across ($78:$52) halved and moved $30 on and projected twice (PROJECT_X_HALF), the first result's logarithm ($70/$71) kept in $AB/$AC.
The distance across ($78:$52) halved, $30 added to its high byte, and projected (PROJECT_X_AT).
A piece's points in the other order, for one driven backwards: $A330 and $8040 swapped end for end, and at every other point the $8080 entry swapped with the one before its mirror.
The piece before the one tried (PIECE_BEHIND), tried instead.

Where the race starts: piece X, or the nearest before it that a car may start on (not a kind with bit 7 at $B240, nor one of the $C779 pieces listed at $0190), into $2E and $C374. The car's state ($0100-$018F) cleared and $2F set to $F0; the piece loaded (PIECE_LOAD); the car put in the middle of the piece's square at height 4, heading the piece's way ($1D EOR $A4, plus $20 for kinds 4 and $0A). The view, the piece, the place across and a step of the physics follow (CAMERA, $9A38, SIDEWAYS, STEP). Then the car's height: $1000 over the road ($0104/$0107), or $C345/$C3D0 doubled plus $18 while the crane holds it ($C37C, with $2F set to $E6); the height over the road at $C35D/$C35E, two of the car's points moved by its turn (TURN_POINTS), the springs at $10 and their speeds cleared ($C343, $C3CE, $C340, $0145), the view again, $C36B $AF and $C36C 8.
Each piece listed at $0190 checked against X.

The distance between the cars round the track: the opponent's piece's distance from the start less the player's ($0670/$06BE, with $C375 and $C374), plus their places along their pieces ($23/$C4 less $22/$C3, over 8). $39/$3A get the shorter of that and the track's length ($C768/$C769) less it; $3B keeps the sign, and $C36A the high byte with bit 7 flipped when the shorter way is the other way round.

A is 0 when both cars are on the same lap ($C378, $C379) and on the same piece counted from the start line ($C374/$C375 less $C77C, round $C764). Otherwise A is the laps' difference, the pieces', or, when those match, the gap's sign $3B; the lamp for who leads reads N.

The boost, while fire is held with the stick pushed forward or back ($66's low two bits, or $C39B bit 7), the car is on the road ($C398 and $0E clear) and there is some left ($C76A, in decimal): every $C388 + 1 passes ($C36E) one is used and the two digits drawn ($44, $45); the flame shown ($72 $80, $6E's low two bits set) and the engine's push doubled ($0150/$0151). Otherwise the flame is off.
A holed part's two cells at Y: the pattern at $80D8, then the one at $80E0 over what was there ANDed with $3F.
A holed part's two cells as they are drawn for the 64 passes after the bump that made the hole: the patterns at $80F8 and $8100.
The cell before a part's two: the pattern at $80E8.
Eight bytes of the bar's patterns from $80C8 + X into the bitmap at $6028 + Y (row 0 of the bitmap at $6000, from column 5), over what is there ANDed with $16; X comes back as Y's cell.
A whole part's two cells: the sixteen bytes at $80C8.
The damage bar drawn afresh: its thirty cells' colour 10 ($D805-$D822), then $C719 whole parts (a gap and two cells, 24 bytes each) and holed ones after them, ten parts in all.

The league's save, made (A bit 7 clear) or read back (set) as a code. Made: the random numbers $02-$06 kept at $801B, and the twelve bytes at $AEB1 (among the drivers' names at $AE00) put at $C700, EOR $3B. Each of the 27 bytes $C700-$C71A is then looked for among the draws of RANDOM from there, and the number of draws it took, two bytes, is what is kept ($8000 high, $8025 low); the random numbers at the end are kept at $8020. Read: the random numbers put back from $801B and the same draws made again, each byte the draw at its count, into $4000; the numbers at the end must match those at $8020, and then the bytes go back to $C700 (with several players, $31A1, only the last three) and to $AEB1. A byte that needs 32,768 draws starts it all again with $03 set to $3B when making the code, and fails a read (carry set). A read with $C77E bit 7 clear does nothing; after either, $C77E is $80.

The controls into $66 (bit 0 forward, 1 back, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire). The five keys at $F807 first, their bits moved to the stick's; with none pressed, the joystick in port 2 ($DC00), and with that idle, outside a race ($3DF8 bit 7 clear), key 8 as fire. RANDOM is drawn on every read, and $F810 counted on when no key is down.
The five keys READ_CONTROLS reads, in the order of $66's bits 4 to 0; the keys menu changes them ($97EB-$986F).
The keys 1 to 4, which pick the line of their number in a menu (MENU_CHOICE, $EED7).
Counted on by READ_CONTROLS when no key is down; the code at $96D4-$9721 uses it as a count too.

Car X has crossed the start line into a lap after its first ($0FDC). While its place along the piece is below $100 ($C3 + X clear), the rest of that first $100 ($22 + X turned over), times 14 over 256 and made decimal, is added to its clock (ADD_TO_CLOCK).

A line steeper than 45 degrees going up to the left, from its lower end (X across, Y down) to the row in A, one pixel a row: the error $0F starts at minus half the rows' distance $52 and gains the columns' $51 each row, a column further left each time it carries. Rows below the view ($C0 on) and columns right of it ($C0 on) are stepped past without drawing, and the end is clipped to the view's top ($40, into $89). Each pixel is the test at $F8C9 (which the game rewrites); the bitmap's byte ($1E/$1F, from the row tables $A500/$A600 and the bitmap's page $12) moves eight bytes left every fourth column, and $138 back every eighth row ($07 the last row before that). A line that goes off the top covers the columns under it (COVER_LEFT).
Past the rows below the view.
Off the left: nothing drawn. Past the columns right of the view.
LINE_UP_LEFT's first pixel's byte in the bitmap.
The next row up: a column left when the error carries, the byte eight back on crossing a byte.

A second test for a pixel, reached when LINE_LIMIT_HIDE has rewritten the branch at $F8D5: drawn only when its row is below $C580 + X and above the column's top ($C600 + X). In the track's test the top has just been set to the row, so there it never draws.

The pixel's test, as LINE_MODE_TRACK or LINE_MODE_CAR writes it from the table at $FC67. The track's: hidden at or below the column's top ($C600 + X), which it then becomes; drawn at or below the limit $0240 + X ($C540 + X once LINE_LIMIT has rewritten the page), else only above $C500 + X. The car's: the column's lowest row kept at $0240 + X; hidden at or below its top ($C600 + X, or $C500 + X after LINE_LIMIT); else drawn, its row kept at $C500 + X.
Loop 1's test for a pixel, 17 bytes to $F8DB, written by LINE_MODE_TRACK and LINE_MODE_CAR from their copies at $FC68 and $FC81; LINE_LIMIT rewrites the page of its second CMP, at $F8D4.
The pixel drawn: the bitmap's byte ANDed with the column's mask ($A400 + X, its low byte set by LINE_COLOUR); the AND is a BIT, drawing nothing, while LINE_OPCODE has it so.
The opcode LINE_OPCODE rewrites: AND ($3D) to draw, BIT ($2C) to cover the columns without drawing. Loop 1 of the four.
The low byte of the AND's mask table, rewritten by LINE_COLOUR: $00 for the masks at $A400, $80 for $A480.
The next row; on leaving the character row, the byte $138 back and $07 eight rows on, unless the end comes first.
At the end: a line that reached the view's top covers the columns from here to its other end (COVER_LEFT).
The columns from X down to A (no further left than $40, no further right than $BF) covered to the top: their tops set to $40, on the page $F92B says ($C6, or $C5 for the car).
The columns from X down to $89 covered the same way.
The page COVER_LEFT_FROM marks the columns on: $C6 for the track, $C5 for the car, written by LINE_MODE_TRACK and LINE_MODE_CAR.

A line steeper than 45 degrees going up to the right, as LINE_UP_LEFT but a column further right each time the error carries, and columns left of the view ($40) stepped past. The test is at $F9D0; a line that goes off the top covers the columns to its other end (COVER_RIGHT_FROM).
LINE_UP_RIGHT past the rows below the view.
Off the right: nothing drawn. Past the columns left of the view.
LINE_UP_RIGHT's first pixel's byte in the bitmap.
The next row up: a column right when the error carries, the byte eight on on crossing a byte.
LINE_UP_RIGHT's second test, as at $F8B9.
LINE_UP_RIGHT's test for the pixel, as at $F8C9.
Loop 2's test for a pixel, 17 bytes written by LINE_MODE_TRACK or LINE_MODE_CAR, its second CMP's page by LINE_LIMIT.
LINE_UP_RIGHT's pixel drawn, as at $F8DC.
Loop 2's opcode, AND or BIT as LINE_OPCODE writes it.
Loop 2's mask table's low byte, from LINE_COLOUR.
The next row, as at $F8E3.
At the end: a line that reached the view's top covers the columns from here to its other end.
The columns from X up to one before $89 covered to the top: their tops set to $40, on the page $FA32 says.
The page COVER_RIGHT_FROM marks the columns on, written by LINE_MODE_TRACK and LINE_MODE_CAR.

A line of 45 degrees or flatter going left from its lower end (X, Y) to the column in A, one pixel a column: the error starts at minus half the columns' distance $51 and gains the rows' $52, a row up each time it carries. Columns right of the view and rows below it are stepped past; the end is clipped at column $40. The test is at $FAD8; the byte moves eight back every fourth column and $138 back on leaving a character row. A line that reaches the view's top covers the columns left to its end (COVER_LEFT_FROM).
Past the columns right of the view.
Above the view: the columns covered. Past the rows below it.
LINE_LEFT's first pixel's byte in the bitmap.
The next column left: a row up when the error carries.
LINE_LEFT's second test, as at $F8B9.
LINE_LEFT's test for the pixel, as at $F8C9.
Loop 3's test for a pixel, 17 bytes written by LINE_MODE_TRACK or LINE_MODE_CAR, its second CMP's page by LINE_LIMIT.
LINE_LEFT's pixel drawn, as at $F8DC.
Loop 3's opcode, AND or BIT as LINE_OPCODE writes it.
Loop 3's mask table's low byte, from LINE_COLOUR.
The next column, and the byte eight back on leaving it, unless the end comes first.
The columns covered (COVER_LEFT_FROM).

A line of 45 degrees or flatter going right, as LINE_LEFT mirrored: columns left of the view stepped past, the end clipped at column $BF, the test at $FBBF, and a line that reaches the top covers the columns right to its end (COVER_RIGHT_FROM).
Past the columns left of the view.
LINE_RIGHT above the view: the columns covered. Past the rows below it.
LINE_RIGHT's first pixel's byte in the bitmap.
The next column right: a row up when the error carries.
LINE_RIGHT's second test, as at $F8B9.
LINE_RIGHT's test for the pixel, as at $F8C9.
Loop 4's test for a pixel, 17 bytes written by LINE_MODE_TRACK or LINE_MODE_CAR, its second CMP's page by LINE_LIMIT.
LINE_RIGHT's pixel drawn, as at $F8DC.
Loop 4's opcode, AND or BIT as LINE_OPCODE writes it.
Loop 4's mask table's low byte, from LINE_COLOUR.
The byte eight on on leaving it, unless the end comes first.
The columns covered (COVER_RIGHT_FROM).
Which mask table the lines draw with: $A400 for X 0, $A480 for X 1 (the low byte from $FC14 + X written into the four loops' ANDs); X kept at $C3AB.
The mask tables' low bytes for LINE_COLOUR.
A written over the four loops' AND ($3D): $2C, a BIT, while the line is only to cover columns, not to be drawn.
The lines set to draw the track: the test for a pixel from $FC68 written into each loop, the columns covered on page $C6, and $C3AD cleared.
The lines set to draw the opponent's car: the view's limits ($C640/$C680) kept at $C540/$C580, the test from $FC81 written into each loop, the columns covered on page $C5, and $C3AD set to $80.
The tests for a pixel that LINE_MODE_TRACK ($FC68-$FC78) and LINE_MODE_CAR ($FC81-$FC91) write into the four loops, seventeen bytes after each loop's CMP, with NOPs between.
LINE_LIMIT, then the branch after the limit's test rewritten to reach the second test ($F8B9 and its like), so that the pixels at or below the limit are hidden.
The page of the second CMP in the four loops' tests rewritten to $C5: the track's test reads its limit from $C540 + X, the car's its top from $C500 + X.
$0280-$02BF copied to $C5C0 and $02C0-$02FF to $C600.

The line from point Y to point X when either is off the screen (a high byte set, $A298/$A2E4). An end above the view's top has its column, clamped to $3F-$C0, at $8B (point Y) or $8C (point X); with both above, the columns between are covered and that is all. Otherwise the distances across and up ($51/$77 and $52/$78, signs at $79/$7A) are halved, their bits into fractions at $7B/$7C, until the larger is below $40, a count at $81 doubling from 1; each end off the screen is walked along the line by those steps until it is on, while the count lasts. When a distance's high byte is bigger, $7D is taken from X, not from $7E. A line whose ends never come on draws nothing, but with $C365 bit 7 its columns are covered. Then the columns under the ends above the top are covered (COVER_ABOVE) and the line drawn from its lower end (LINE_FROM_ENDS).
Both ends' distances.
Halved until the larger is below $40.
The steps ran out.
Point Y walked on, until it is on the screen.
The walk's test: end Y ($4F/$50) is on the screen once both its high bytes ($73, $74) are 0, and until then it is walked on (CLIP_WALK_Y). From $FE50 the same test for end X ($75, $76).
Point X walked back, until it is on the screen.
For each end that was above the view's top ($8B for the end at $4F, $8C for the one at $4E), the columns between its clamped column and the end as it now is covered (COVER_LEFT).
The line between points X and Y, unless either is behind the eye ($A330 bit 7): LINE_ON_SCREEN when both are on the screen, otherwise LINE_CLIP.
The columns of points X and Y added to the span $60-$61, then LINE_ON_SCREEN.
The line between points X and Y, both on the screen: the lower end into $4F/$50 and the upper into $4E/$8A, then LINE_FROM_ENDS.

The line from its lower end ($4F, $50) to its upper ($4E, $8A). For the car ($C3AD bit 7), with either end at or below the view's bottom ($C0), the lowest rows ($0240) of the columns between set to $C0 first. Then the distances ($51, $52) and the loop for the line's way: LINE_RIGHT, LINE_UP_RIGHT, LINE_LEFT or LINE_UP_LEFT.
The distances, and which loop.
An RTS that no code reaches.
The piece on the square $0B across and $0C along from the view's square ($5C, $5E) (PIECE_FROM_HERE); carry set when that is off the map.
The KERNAL's CINT, which SAVE_OR_LOAD calls with the KERNAL banked in ($2B47). With the KERNAL out these bytes are SQUARE_PIECE's.

The KERNAL's IOINIT, which SAVE_OR_LOAD calls with the KERNAL banked in ($2B35), as it calls RAMTAS ($FF87), VECTOR ($FF8D), CINT ($FF81) and SETMSG ($FF90). With the KERNAL out these bytes are SQUARE_PIECE's.
The KERNAL's RAMTAS, called with it banked in ($2B3C).
The KERNAL's VECTOR, called with it banked in ($2B44, and at the start-up).
Puts A in $15 and runs on into LOAD_14. Callers use it to start a two-byte sum: the high byte goes to $15, the low comes back in A with the carry clear.
Loads $14 into A and clears the carry.
The road's height under the opponent's point X (ROAD_HEIGHT_AT), an eighth of it, into $07EC/$07F0.

The front wheels' top halves stepped on by a frame, so the tyres seem to roll: called from the interrupt each time the engine's count $5F carries, it steps the right wheel's sprite 7 through frames $60-$62 and the left's sprite 5 through $65-$67, one way round while the speed along the road ($0159) is positive and the other while it is negative. This is the game's own code, in the RAM under the KERNAL ROM; the disk routines ($2B51-$2BCC, $90C7-$90FF) call $FFB7, $FFBA, $FFBD, $FFC3 and $FFD5 with the ROM switched in, and reach the KERNAL's READST, SETLFS, SETNAM, CLOSE and LOAD instead.
The KERNAL's READST, called with it banked in ($2BCC). With the KERNAL out these bytes are WHEELS_TURN's.
The KERNAL's SETLFS, called with it banked in.
The KERNAL's SETNAM, called with it banked in.
The KERNAL's OPEN, which DISK_COMMAND calls with the KERNAL banked in ($90EF). With the KERNAL out these bytes are WHEELS_TURN's.
The KERNAL's CLOSE, called with it banked in (DISK_COMMAND).
The KERNAL's LOAD, called with it banked in ($2BC6).
The KERNAL's SAVE, which SAVE_OR_LOAD calls with the KERNAL banked in ($2BB3). With the KERNAL out these bytes are WHEELS_TURN's.
The wheels' new frames into sprite pointers 7 and 5 ($5FFF, $5FFD).
